stories.title: Yogi says one took exam, another got the job:'Munna Bhais' were sitting in the system; 1,146 candidates receive joining letters
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said on Wednesday that before 2017, young people could not get government jobs fairly in the state. He said there was discrimination in the recruitment process and that appointment boards and commissions were under the control of the Saifai syndicate. Yogi said that people known as 'Munna Bhais' had even taken control of government positions. He said, "Before 2017, one person would take the examination, while someone else would get the appointment letter." Earlier, the Chief Minister distributed appointment letters to 1,146 candidates selected for junior assistant posts in the Revenue Department in Lucknow. He also provided financial assistance worth ₹215 crore to 4,300 beneficiaries under the Chief Minister's Farmer Accident Welfare Scheme. Key points from Yogi's speech 1. Yogi asks candidates if they had to pay money or seek recommendations After handing over the appointment letters, Yogi asked the candidates whether they had to seek recommendations from anyone during the recruitment process. He also asked if anyone had asked them for money, called them to influence the process or created problems during document verification. All the candidates replied that they had faced no such problems. Yogi said this showed the progress made by Uttar Pradesh. 2. Those in the government were behind the unfair practices earlier Yogi said it was unfair when a person who did not even take an examination got an appointment letter, while deserving candidates who worked hard were left without jobs. He said candidates naturally felt hurt when they did not get the results of their hard work. They would complain to the government or approach the court, but the same government was responsible for these unfair practices. This often led to court cases and stay orders. 3. SP government had also disbanded 34 PAC companies The Chief Minister said that when his government came to power in 2017, he held a meeting with the police and Home Department officials. He asked how many posts were vacant in the police force. Officials told him that around 1.5 lakh posts were vacant at the time. Yogi also said that the Samajwadi Party government had disbanded 34 companies of the Provincial Armed Constabulary (PAC), which was known for taking action against rioters. He claimed that around 1,500 riots took place during the SP government's rule. News being updated…

stories.title: Man shoots himself at girlfriend's house:Family refused to let them meet; her marriage fixed with someone else
stories.summary: A 30-year-old man died by suicide after shooting himself outside his girlfriend's house in Basti on Wednesday morning. The girl's family had initially agreed to their relationship but later refused to go ahead with the marriage and fixed her marriage with someone else. At around 7:30 am, Shiv arrived at the girl's house to meet her, but her family stopped him outside. He said that he would kill himself if they did not let him meet her. When the family refused, he took out a country-made pistol and shot himself in the chest. The incident took place in Basewa Rai village in Harraiya, around 30 km from the district headquarters. After receiving information, the police and forensic team reached the spot and collected evidence. Police questioned the family, took custody of the body and sent it for a post-mortem examination. He created a scene in the village before shooting himself According to the police, Shivkumar, a resident of Thakurpur, had come to Basewa Rai village to visit his relative, Lalu Prasad. He was in a relationship with a girl from the family and was insisting on meeting her. When he could not meet her, he threatened to die by suicide. Shivkumar was shouting loudly, hearing which people from nearby houses gathered at the spot and tried to calm him down. However, he did not listen to anyone and shot himself in front of the villagers. Amid the chaos, Harraiya Station House Officer Sanjay Kumar reached the spot with police personnel and a forensic team. The officer said that the marriage of the two had been fixed earlier but was called off for some reason. He said this led Shivkumar to die by suicide. However, Circle Officer Swarnima Singh gave a different account. She said Shivkumar wanted to marry his cousin, his paternal aunt's daughter, but the girl was not willing to marry him. This had led to tension between the two families. On Wednesday, Shivkumar threatened people before shooting himself. Here is the full sequence of events According to Parshurampur police station in-charge Pradeep Singh, Shivkumar was a resident of Thakurpur village and had been in a relationship with a young woman from Basewa village. The two had been in contact for the past 10 years. Shivkumar wanted to marry the woman at any cost. However, after her family fixed her marriage elsewhere, he allegedly sent them objectionable photos and videos of her and threatened to make them public. After receiving a complaint, Parshurampur police called both of them to the police station on Tuesday, a day before the incident. They reached an agreement and decided to stop talking to each other and change their mobile numbers. Shivkumar also agreed to delete the photos and videos from his phone. However, the very next day, he reached the woman's house and insisted on meeting her. He started shouting loudly and later shot himself.

stories.title: House wall collapses, killing 2 children:Trapped under debris while sleeping with parents, bodies recovered after 7 hours
stories.summary: Two young sisters died after a wall of their house collapsed in Varanasi, while their parents were injured. The family was sleeping in the verandah of their house, which was built beside a pond, when the accident occurred. The wall suddenly collapsed at around 12.30 am on Tuesday night, trapping the entire family under the debris. Water from the pond also flooded the house following the collapse. The parents somehow managed to get out, but the two girls remained trapped under the debris and water. Hearing their cries, neighbours woke up and rushed to the spot. Police and State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) teams arrived and launched a rescue operation. After seven hours, at around 7.30 am, the bodies of Afiya (7) and Palak (4) were recovered from the debris. Their mother, Tabassum, and father, Ajuddin, were inconsolable after seeing their daughters' bodies. Police said moisture and dampness in the house, due to its location beside the pond, may have contributed to the collapse. The incident took place in the Bachchhaw Pashchim Pura area under the Rohania police station limits. Grandfather recounts how the accident happened The girls' grandfather, Sirajuddin, said the family had gone to sleep at night. His son, daughter-in-law and four children were inside the house, while he was sleeping outside. "I woke up when the wall suddenly collapsed. I heard my son and daughter-in-law shouting, 'The children have drowned, the children have drowned!'" He said he immediately jumped into the pond. Other villagers soon reached the spot, and his brother also jumped into the water to search for the children. However, they could not find them. The police arrived later and began the search operation. Sirajuddin said two children died in the accident, while the family's elder daughter, Roshni, and a younger son survived. The boy has not yet been named. He added that the family owns the land and has the property registration documents. The house was built in 2010. Family lived in a four-room house Sirajuddin's house has four rooms and a tin shed at the front. He has three sons. His eldest son, Ajuddin alias Kallu, is married, while his two younger sons are unmarried. Ajuddin lived in one of the rooms with his wife and their four children, making a family of six. Rohania ACP Awadhesh Vishwakarma said two girls died after the wall collapsed. Police reached the spot during the night after receiving information and called in rescue teams. Both bodies were recovered from the debris. Further action is being taken in the case.

stories.title: Muslim Christian groups accused of religious conversions in Lucknow:Hindu woman doctor targeted; former DGP claims bid to establish 'Ghazwa-e-Hind'
stories.summary: Several cases of alleged religious conversion have come to light in Lucknow over the past few months. A preliminary investigation is said to have pointed to the involvement of some Christian missionaries and Muslim organisations. Hindu organisations have alleged that some Muslim men target Hindu girls and women by trapping them in relationships under the name of 'love jihad'. They then pressure them to change their religion. Christian missionaries are also accused of using prayer meetings to attract poor Hindu families by offering financial help and claiming to cure illnesses. They allegedly persuade people to convert gradually. Former DGP links 'love jihad' to attempts to create terrorists Former Director General of Police Brij Lal said attempts were being made to create terrorists through 'love jihad' to carry out 'Ghazwa-e-Hind', which he described as a religious war against India. He also said that those questioning the Special Task Force (STF) investigation should themselves be investigated. He called for strict action against them so that it sets an example. Meanwhile, Hindu Mahasabha national spokesperson Shishir Chaturvedi said that King George's Medical University (KGMU) no longer appeared to be just a hospital. He alleged that it had become a place where Hindu girls were being targeted. He also demanded an investigation into the role of KGMU officials in the matter. Check out the pictures below : First, understand Muslim love jihad Hindu girls targeted, rate cards prepared The STF established during its investigation into KGMU doctor Rameez and those linked to him that Hindu girls were targeted and converted by forming a gang. Rate cards were also prepared to target girls from different castes. Doctors with good physiques were also provided facilities to influence the girls. Maulanas trained them to appear secular and to make the girls feel safe before luring them. Nursing staff at KGMU lured and converted The STF has stated in connection with the case that came to light in the conversion racket operating at KGMU that some doctors and employees posted in the pathology and other departments used to lure Hindu women doctors, students and nursing staff into romantic relationships and subject them to physical and mental exploitation. They later pressured them to convert. Prof. Suresh Babu, head of the pathology department, Dr Sumaira Qayoom and others used to suppress such cases, side with the accused and discriminate against Hindu employees and doctors. Parents of accused Dr Rameez also used to brainwash people The charge sheet filed by the police in the case involving Dr Ramizuddin, alias Ramiz, states that the main accused in the KGMU conversion case, Dr Ramizuddin alias Ramiz, and his parents used to brainwash and trap non-Muslim women doctors. They would initially pretend to be secular. They would then pose as hardline Muslims, make obscene videos and photographs to carry out religious conversions, and subsequently torture the victims. His parents allegedly drugged a woman doctor and had their son, Dr Ramiz, rape her. Two women doctors were allegedly forced to undergo abortions. Now, understand Christian conversion in the name of healing meetings... Contacting people through religious gatherings Although the allegation of religious conversion linked to the prayer meeting held inside a house in Rajajipuram has not been substantiated in the police's preliminary investigation, the method of inviting people to the meeting and assuring them that their personal problems would be resolved is similar to that seen in earlier cases. Investigations into religious conversion cases in Nigohan and Mohanlalganj had also found that problems such as illness, poverty and childlessness were being used to establish contact with people. A case of religious conversion in the name of a healing meeting came to light in September 2025 in Baktaurikheda village of Nigohan. Police arrested Malkhan alias Mathews. He was accused of inviting people to the meeting by assuring them that their illnesses would be cured and financial problems resolved. The investigation also found that contact with people was being expanded through religious meetings. Claim of financial assistance and treatment for illnesses Similarly, a religious conversion case came to light in July 2026 in Bharsawan village in Mohanlalganj. Police have filed a charge sheet against seven accused in the case. The police investigation found that people were being offered various inducements, including treatment for illnesses, the prospect of having children, financial assistance and education for their children. The gang lured people with money. After this, meetings were held at night, after which people were misled into becoming crypto-Christians, or secret Christians. The investigation also found that the gang did not ask people to change their names. After one generation, the next-or the third generation-became completely Christian, and their names were then changed. Healing meeting being held at a house on 1 November Information has emerged that prayer meetings were held every Sunday at a house in D-3, Rajajipuram, with the meeting on 1 November also taking place there. Women, men and children from various areas, including Dubagga, Kakori and Mohan, used to attend. Police sources said that during questioning, those who attended the meeting told them that they were promised relief from illness and poverty and the blessing of having children, among other things. Vishwa Hindu Parishad vice-president Saroj Singh said that more than 100 women, men and children were seated at the prayer meeting. The women said they had been called there to accept Christianity and that this would rid them of their sorrow and problems. That was why they had come there. However, Talकटora police said that the preliminary investigation had found no evidence of religious conversion. Bajrang Dal and Vishva Hindu Parishad members said that, as in earlier cases, a conversion racket was being run here by offering inducements. The police should investigate the matter seriously.

stories.title: Former GST Commissioner Anupama likes Sitapur:Says Akhilesh-Dimple are her favourite couple; has also written songs for Rahat Fateh Ali Khan
stories.summary: Anupama Saroj Singh, a Provincial Civil Services (PCS) officer who served as Deputy Commissioner (GST) in the Uttar Pradesh government, has taken voluntary retirement from service. She has since sought a Samajwadi Party ticket to contest the Assembly election from the Sidhauli seat in Sitapur. Anupama says she has entered politics to challenge the barriers in society that prevent people from bringing about change. She also said she admires the partnership between Akhilesh Yadav and Dimple Yadav, as they complement each other. This is one of the reasons she is drawn to the Samajwadi Party. Asked where she plans to contest the election, she said she has a deep emotional connection with Sitapur. Anupama is the wife of Samajwadi Party national spokesperson Anurag Bhadauria and the daughter of former MP Sushila Saroj. Her mother has served as a Lok Sabha MP and was also a minister in the Mulayam Singh Yadav government. Her husband has contested the Lucknow East Assembly seat and served as a minister in the Akhilesh Yadav government. Anupama is also a singer and composer. Anupama talks about her musical journey and favourite singers In an exclusive conversation with a Dainik Bhaskar reporter, Anupama spoke about her interest in music. She said Rahat Fateh Ali Khan is her favourite singer and that she has composed several songs for him, which he has also sung. She also enjoys Sonu Nigam's music. Among contemporary singers, she likes Arijit Singh's songs, although she has not yet had the opportunity to work with him. Read the full conversation with Anupama - Question: How are you feeling after leaving your job? Answer: I am feeling quite free from stress. I am spending time with my family during the festival. The word retirement itself means being free from work. However, I still have a great deal of responsibility and many challenges ahead of me. I am now quite excited about this new journey, as I have a lot to do there. I have an open sky before me. Question: You have taken VRS, and since then, speculation about you entering politics has intensified? Answer: Politics is a very broad term. It can be a means of connecting with society, but that is not my primary objective. My main aim is to break the barriers that make people feel uncomfortable about connecting with society. I have some ideas of my own and want to work on them. I want to improve the things around me. I now feel free from constraints; it feels as though there is a canvas in front of me that I have to fill with colour. In our family, my mother and maternal grandfather were involved in politics and served society through it. I simply want to take that work forward. Question: You come from a political background and resigned just before the election. Will you contest the 2027 election? Answer: I am not in a position right now to reveal anything or say whether I will contest an election or enter politics in the future. I have many thoughts and feel deeply for the people. When I feel the time is right to use my administrative experience and energy to help improve society, a decision will be taken. Question: Recently, IAS officer Divya Mittal left her job and entered politics. Has politics gained the upper hand over the bureaucracy? Answer: I would not say that politics has gained the upper hand over the bureaucracy. Everyone has their own priorities and perspective. People leave their jobs for personal reasons. There is no political pressure. Yes, politics is certainly connected to all our lives. People have moved from the bureaucracy to the corporate sector or other sectors; not everyone enters politics. Question: Do you have a preferred constituency from which you would like to contest the election? Answer: (Laughing) I like the whole of India. I am a daughter of India, and I will contest from wherever fate decides. We will see what happens from there. My mother contested from Mohanlalganj, and we campaigned for her during our childhood. We also have a deep connection with Sitapur. We have observed politics closely since childhood. However, no decision of this kind has been taken yet. I also like music very much. We have composed songs for Rahat Fateh Ali Khan and Mika Singh. They have sung our songs. Music is my soul. You may hear my songs on social issues in the future. Question: Who is your favourite singer? Answer: Rahat Fateh Ali Khan. I have written songs for him. Apart from him, I also like Sonu Nigam very much. Among young artists, I particularly like Arijit Singh. It has been my misfortune that I have not yet been able to work with him. Question: Which political personality do you like the most? Answer: Atal Bihari Vajpayee and Mulayam Singh are among my favourite leaders. We have had a close family relationship with Mulayam Singh. I particularly like Atal ji's thinking and the way he spoke, especially his poetry. Among women, I like Dimple Yadav very much; her way of speaking and simplicity have deeply impressed me. It is her simplicity that takes her family forward. Question: We are living in the Gen Z era. How do you view it? Answer: The Gen Z movement that has emerged is a symbol that our country needs change. We were looking at the countries around us and sensing that this movement would now reach India. We saw that the issues affecting the countries around us were the same issues affecting our country. We saw that change was needed. Gen Z is the largest population group in our country, and its members will make sure they achieve what they want. At a time like this, the new generation should come forward, and whatever change takes place will be brought about by Gen Z. Question: There is a lot of talk about couples in politics. Who is your favourite couple? Answer: We see only one couple in politics: Akhilesh Yadav and Dimple Yadav. They complement each other very well. The values they uphold are also reflected in the party. They consider their party workers members of their family, and all the workers address them as Bhaiya and Bhabhi.

stories.title: Former MP Rajesh Mishra eyes PM Modi's Varanasi seat:Puts up posters signalling 2029 Lok Sabha bid after joining BJP from Congress
stories.summary: A poster featuring former MP Rajesh Mishra has triggered political discussions in Varanasi ahead of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. The former Congress leader, who joined the BJP, has signalled his intention to contest the 2029 Lok Sabha elections from Varanasi. Mishra has staked his claim to the seat represented by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who has won it three consecutive times. He has released a poster featuring the BJP's lotus symbol and shared it on his social media accounts. His move to stake a claim to the Varanasi seat has sparked discussions within the BJP. His supporters have also posted comments expressing their support, while BJP leaders have largely avoided commenting on the development. On Tuesday night, former MP Rajesh Mishra changed his display picture and cover photo on Facebook and X, triggering discussions in Varanasi and national political circles. The poster projects him as a strong contender for the BJP ticket from Varanasi in 2029. This is the first time a BJP leader has publicly staked a claim to the seat represented by the Prime Minister, drawing attention in both BJP and opposition circles. The party may also view Mishra's social media post as a matter of indiscipline. Rajesh Mishra joined BJP three years ago Former Varanasi MP Dr Rajesh Mishra joined the BJP three years ago. At the party's central office in Delhi, former Union Minister Ravi Shankar Prasad inducted him as a primary member of the BJP. Mishra had said that opposition parties would not even find polling agents for their candidates in the Varanasi constituency. He had also described it as a matter of pride that Narendra Modi represented Varanasi and had brought recognition to the city and the country worldwide. Rajesh Mishra represented Varanasi in 2004 Rajesh Mishra is known as a soft-spoken politician in Varanasi. He began his political journey through student politics at Banaras Hindu University (BHU). In the 1980s, he was elected president of the BHU Students' Union. From 1996 to 2004, he served two terms as a member of the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council (MLC). In the 1999 Lok Sabha elections, the Congress fielded him against BJP candidate Shankar Prasad Jaiswal from Varanasi. Mishra lost that election but defeated Jaiswal in 2004 to win the Varanasi Lok Sabha seat. Lost to Murli Manohar Joshi in 2009 The Congress fielded Mishra for the third consecutive time in 2009. The BJP nominated Dr Murli Manohar Joshi, while Mukhtar Ansari contested on a BSP ticket. After falling out with the BJP, Ajay Rai contested the election on a Samajwadi Party ticket. Vote polarisation is believed to have pushed Mishra down to fourth place. Joshi secured 2,03,122 votes, Mukhtar Ansari received 1,85,911, Ajay Rai got 1,23,874, while Mishra secured 66,386 votes. Expressed displeasure after being denied ticket in 2014 In 2014, the Congress dropped Mishra and fielded Ajay Rai against Narendra Modi, then the BJP's prime ministerial candidate. Three years later, the Varanasi South Assembly constituency became a major political talking point during the 2017 Assembly elections. The BJP's decision to deny a ticket to seven-time MLA Shyamdev Roy Chowdhury, popularly known as Dada, had created difficulties for the party. The BJP fielded Neelkanth Tiwari, while the Congress nominated Rajesh Mishra against him. Prime Minister Narendra Modi stayed in Varanasi and campaigned during the election. Tiwari defeated Mishra. In the 2019 Lok Sabha elections, the Congress again gave Mishra a ticket, this time from Salempur in his home district of Deoria. However, he secured only 27,288 votes and lost his security deposit. Poster creates buzz amid Assembly election discussions Rajesh Mishra represented Varanasi in the Lok Sabha from 2004 to 2009. There had been discussions about fielding him from Bhadohi or another constituency in the Assembly elections when his poster staking a claim to the 2029 Varanasi Lok Sabha ticket surfaced. Mishra's decision to join the BJP had been a major setback for the Congress. He was reportedly unhappy with Ajay Rai's appointment as the state Congress president. However, following Rai's removal, speculation has also emerged about Mishra potentially returning to the Congress. There is also speculation over whether PM Modi will contest the next Lok Sabha election from Varanasi or retire from electoral politics there. Political observers are interpreting Mishra's poster as a possible calculated political move. Mishra yet to get a significant position in BJP Despite joining the BJP from the Congress, Mishra has not received a prominent organisational position in the party, according to the report. His political influence is also said to have declined over the past three years. Several of his former associates have reportedly distanced themselves from him, while his role within the BJP has remained limited. During the Prime Minister's visits, Mishra has reportedly been seen among those welcoming him from behind barricades.

stories.title: Air quality worsens in Noida-Ghaziabad, AQI crosses 300:Fog covers western UP districts; temperatures to drop in 2 days
stories.summary: Fog and haze have increased across Uttar Pradesh after Diwali. The Meteorological Department has issued an alert for dense fog in the state on Wednesday. Temperatures are also expected to drop, with severe cold likely to begin after two days. Visibility dropped to zero in Varanasi on Tuesday morning due to dense fog. In Bareilly, visibility was limited to 100 metres, while it was 300 metres in the state capital, Lucknow. Dense fog also covered 15 cities, including Sambhal, Hapur, Bijnor and Shamli. Hardoi and Bareilly were the coldest places, with minimum temperatures of 13.5°C and 14.2°C, respectively. BHU meteorologist Prof. Manoj Srivastava said, "Minimum temperatures will fall further as dry north-westerly winds become stronger. This will make the cold more intense." Weather in four major districts - Lucknow: Cold conditions have increased in the city. Light fog was seen in the morning, while the air quality remained poor. The AQI was recorded at 200. - Kanpur: Cold winds have been blowing since morning, and light mist was seen on the roads. Weather expert Dr S.N. Sunil Pandey said sunshine would cause temperatures to rise during the day, but it would remain cold at night. - Varanasi: The weather remained clear in the city, but haze was visible after Diwali fireworks. Humidity in the air also made the weather feel cold. - Prayagraj: The weather remained clear, but strong winds made it feel cold. Dense fog continued in rural areas, while mist was seen in the city. Know the temperatures recorded over the past 24 hours What is the Air Quality Index (AQI)? It is a score that indicates the quality of the air and helps us understand whether the air around us is clean or polluted. The AQI measures the levels of pollutants present in the air. The higher the AQI, the more dangerous the air is considered to be, and the greater the health risk. Understand it through the graphic below- How does poor AQI affect our health? When the AQI is poor, pollutants such as PM2.5, PM10, nitrogen dioxide, sulphur dioxide and ozone present in the air reach deep into our lungs. These particles spread throughout the body through the bloodstream. They can cause various health problems, ranging from immediate effects to long-term conditions. stories.title: 3 more special trains to run via Gorakhpur for Chhath:Travel to Delhi, Bihar, Mumbai to become easier; check dates timings
stories.summary: Railways has announced three additional special train services to manage the rush of passengers travelling home for Chhath after Diwali and returning to work. These trains will run between Muzaffarpur and Delhi, Ramnagar and Patliputra, and Mumbai and Gorakhpur. A festival special train will make one trip between Muzaffarpur and Anand Vihar Terminal via Gorakhpur. The running period of the Ramnagar-Patliputra weekly special train has also been extended, with one additional trip planned. Meanwhile, a 20-coach special train will run between Mumbai's Lokmanya Tilak Terminus and Gorakhpur from November 10. These services will make travel easier for passengers travelling to and from Bihar, eastern Uttar Pradesh, Lucknow, Delhi and Mumbai. Special train from Muzaffarpur to Delhi on November 18 Train number 05281, the Muzaffarpur-Anand Vihar Terminal Festival Special, will leave Muzaffarpur at 6:30 am on November 18. It will reach Gorakhpur at 3 pm after stopping at Motipur, Mehsi, Chakia, Pipra, Bapudham Motihari, Sagauli, Bettiah, Narkatiaganj, Harinagar and Bagaha. From Gorakhpur, it will travel via Basti, Gonda, Lucknow, Hardoi, Shahjahanpur and Moradabad before reaching Anand Vihar Terminal at 5 am the next day. On the return journey, train number 05282 will leave Anand Vihar Terminal at 7 am on November 19. It will pass through Moradabad, Shahjahanpur, Hardoi and Lucknow before reaching Gonda at 6:05 pm, Basti at 7:30 pm and Gorakhpur at 9:10 pm. From Gorakhpur, it will travel via Bagaha, Harinagar, Narkatiaganj, Bettiah, Sagauli, Bapudham Motihari, Pipra, Chakia, Mehsi and Motipur. It will reach Muzaffarpur at 4:50 am the next day. The train will have 22 coaches, including 10 AC three-tier coaches, six sleeper coaches, four general second-class coaches, one generator-cum-luggage van and one LSLRD coach. One additional trip for Ramnagar-Patliputra Special Railways has extended the running period of the 05080/05079 Ramnagar-Patliputra-Ramnagar weekly special train. Train number 05080 will make one additional trip from Ramnagar to Patliputra on November 28. On the return journey, train number 05079 will run from Patliputra to Ramnagar on November 29. The train will pass through Gorakhpur. Its route, stoppages, timings and coach arrangement will remain unchanged. This will help passengers from Gorakhpur and nearby areas travel to Bihar. 20-coach special train between Mumbai and Gorakhpur from November 10 Railways is also operating the 01027/01028 festival special train between Lokmanya Tilak Terminus in Mumbai and Gorakhpur. Train number 01027 will leave Lokmanya Tilak Terminus at 2:50 pm on November 10. It will pass through Thane, Kalyan, Igatpuri, Nashik Road, Bhusawal, Khandwa, Itarsi, Bhopal, Bina, Veerangana Lakshmibai Jhansi, Orai, Kanpur Central, Lucknow, Barabanki, Gonda, Mankapur, Basti and Khalilabad before reaching Gorakhpur at 11:50 pm. On the return journey, train number 01028 will leave Gorakhpur at 5:30 am on November 12. It will pass through Khalilabad, Basti, Mankapur, Gonda, Barabanki, Lucknow, Kanpur Central, Orai, Jhansi, Bina and Bhopal. It will then travel via Itarsi, Khandwa, Bhusawal, Nashik Road, Igatpuri, Kalyan and Thane before reaching Lokmanya Tilak Terminus at 2:30 pm the next day. The train will have 20 coaches, including 10 sleeper coaches, five AC three-tier economy coaches, one AC two-tier coach, two general second-class coaches, one generator-cum-luggage van and one LSLRD coach. These three services will provide more travel options to passengers during the Chhath festival rush. They are expected to help passengers travelling via Gorakhpur towards Bihar, Delhi and Mumbai.

stories.title: Shopkeeper shot dead in Ghazipur market:Chased attacker before collapsing, struggled for life on road for 5 minutes, cried for help
stories.summary: A young man was shot dead in the middle of a market in Ghazipur on Tuesday evening (November 10). He ran a footwear shop and was returning home when a man in a car rammed into his motorbike, causing him to fall. The attacker then fired three rounds at him. One bullet struck the victim on the left side of his neck, while another hit his abdomen. Despite being injured, he ran about 20 metres behind the attacker's car before collapsing on the road. Victim names Shubham as shooter before collapsing As he lay injured, the young man repeatedly took Shubham's name and shouted, "Shubham has shot me, save me." Local residents immediately rushed him to hospital, where he died during treatment. DIG of the Varanasi zone Vaibhav Krishna also reached the spot and sought details of the incident from officials. Police suspect old enmity behind the murder According to the police, Shubham and the footwear shop owner had an old dispute. Two days before the shooting, Shubham had lodged a complaint with the police, alleging that the shopkeeper had thrown a bomb at him and attempted to kill him. The deceased was his parents' only son. See 2 pictures... Read the full story... Mohammad Daud lives in the Muftipura neighbourhood with his only son, 28-year-old Mohammad Kausen. Kausen ran a footwear shop in the Rauza area. The family of Anil Chaubey, who has since died, lives near the Niyazi Ganga Temple, around 3 km away. His son, Shubham Chaubey, lives at the house. On November 8, Shubham lodged a police complaint alleging that Kausen had thrown a bomb at him and attempted to kill him. On Tuesday, Kausen had gone to Mishra Bazaar to eat samosas. Shortly after leaving the area on his motorcycle, he was near the State Bank when Shubham allegedly rammed his vehicle into the bike. He collided with an e-rickshaw and fell on the road. Shubham then opened fire, hitting him with two bullets and leaving him critically injured. Local residents alerted an ambulance and rushed Kausen to hospital. Despite receiving treatment, he died. Following Kausen's death, his father, Mohammad Daud, accused Shubham Chaubey of murdering his son. Case was registered against Kausen in 2025 Vaibhav Krishna, DIG of the Varanasi Range, who reached the scene, said that Shubham and Kausen had an old rivalry. A case was registered in 2025 involving Kausen and Shubham's father, Anil Chaubey. Kausen was accused of firing a shot in the case. The police also filed a charge sheet. The DIG said that a case had been registered against Shubham.

stories.title: Who will carry forward Azam Khan's legacy in 2027?:Abdullah's path remains difficult despite SC relief; focus shifts to wife Tanjin, elder son Adeeb and daughter-in-law
stories.summary: The date of 17 November 2026 proved lucky for the Azam family. First, the Supreme Court granted relief to wife Tazeen Fatma and younger son Abdullah in the fake birth certificate case. Then, by evening, the Allahabad High Court also granted interim bail to Azam Khan in a money laundering case. Following this, the question has begun to arise whether Azam Khan or his son Abdullah will be able to contest the 2027 UP Assembly elections? Legal experts say—Azam Khan has been sentenced to 2 to 10 years in 8 cases against him. Therefore, he cannot contest elections. Abdullah has certainly received relief in the fake birth certificate case, but due to convictions in two other cases, he too will not be able to contest elections. Tazeen Fatma can contest elections. However, considering her age and health, the names of elder son Adeeb and daughter-in-law Sidra are being discussed more. In such a situation, who from the Azam family can enter the fray in the 2027 elections? What are the legal hurdles before whom, and what options does the family have? Understand in this report… Abdullah Azam, who has been a two-time MLA from Rampur's Suar seat, has a total of 46 criminal cases registered against him. Out of these, he has been convicted by a magistrate court in four cases, while hearings are still underway in 42 cases. One of these four cases is of a fake passport. In December 2025, the magistrate court sentenced him to seven years in this case. However, in May 2026, the sessions court cancelled his sentence. Now on 17 November 2026, the Supreme Court also stayed the verdict convicting him in the fake birth certificate case. Even after getting relief in these two cases, the path for Abdullah to contest elections is not clear yet. There are two major reasons for this— 1. Two PAN cards case: On 17 November 2025, Rampur's MP-MLA court sentenced Abdullah to seven years in jail in the case of possessing two PAN cards. The sessions court had also rejected his appeal. On 29 October 2026, the Allahabad High Court granted him bail, but refused to stay the verdict convicting him. 2. Chhajlet (Moradabad) case: In February 2023, a Moradabad court sentenced Abdullah to 2 years in jail in a 15-year-old highway blockade case. Following this, he lost his legislative membership. The verdict convicting him in this case also stands intact. Stay on conviction and bail, then why can't they contest elections Senior advocate in the Supreme Court, Shariq Abbasi, says—merely getting bail does not make a person eligible to contest elections. When a lower court sentences someone, an application can be filed in the higher court along with the appeal to stay the sentence and stay the conviction. A stay on conviction is necessary to contest elections. No hurdle in wife Tazeen contesting elections, but age is advancing Around a dozen cases, including land grabbing of Jauhar University, electricity theft at Humsafar Resort, and fake birth certificate, were registered against former Rajya Sabha MP and former Rampur MLA Dr Tazeen Fatma. Tazeen Fatma has so far been sentenced in only one case, the fake birth certificate case. In October 2023, Rampur's MP-MLA court sentenced her to 7 years in jail. In May 2024, the High Court granted her bail, but did not stay the verdict convicting her. Now, on 17 November 2026, a Supreme Court bench of Justice Dipankar Datta and Justice Sheel Nagu has also stayed her conviction. She has not been sentenced to two years or more in any other case. In such a situation, based on this information, there currently appears to be no bar on her contesting elections. However, she is over 75 years old. Health-related issues and ongoing hearings in other cases could pose a challenge for her. Elder son eligible to contest elections, but less interest in politics Azam Khan's elder son Adeeb Azam has always stayed away from active politics. He manages his business in Noida and Delhi. He was sent notices in a few cases of land disputes related to Jauhar University. Leaving aside the initial FIRs, he has neither been convicted in any other case nor found guilty in any serious criminal matter. Legally, Adeeb is eligible to contest elections. In recent months, when Azam Khan was in jail, Adeeb came before the media and was also seen interacting with supporters. However, Adeeb has not had a direct role in Rampur's politics. He does not have the same grip among party workers and local voters as Azam Khan or Abdullah Azam have had. Whom can SP field for the 2027 elections from the Azam family After the legal situation is clear, Akhilesh Yadav may field Dr Tazeen Fatma in the electoral fray from Rampur Sadar or Suar seat. In the 2019 by-election, she was elected MLA from the Rampur Sadar seat. Thus, she has experience in contesting elections and electoral strategy. If Tazeen Fatma is unable to contest elections due to health reasons or any other legal hurdle, then elder son Adeeb Azam could be the second option to carry forward the family's political legacy. Adeeb's wife Sidra, the daughter-in-law of Azam Khan, is also eligible to contest elections. There is no legal case of any kind against her either. Is Azam Khan's political grip weakening in his own stronghold? Since Azam Khan went to jail, the political equations of Rampur have changed rapidly. On one hand, the BJP has strengthened its hold on the Rampur Sadar seat, from where Akash Saxena is the MLA. Meanwhile, NDA ally Apna Dal (S) holds the Suar seat, whereas the Chamraua seat is currently with the Samajwadi Party. In Rampur, whose politics revolved solely around 'Azam Khan' for decades, the balance of power has now completely changed. On one hand, the NDA has expanded its base by breaching Azam's fortress, once considered impregnable, through by-elections; on the other hand, Mohibbullah Nadvi's victory in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections worked to give a new lease of life to the SP in Rampur. However, the internal tug-of-war between the Azam faction and MP Nadvi has posed a new challenge before the Samajwadi Party. Now, the political battle of Rampur is not just about stopping the BJP, but also about whose hands the real command of the SP will remain in within the district.

stories.title: UP tops cybercrime, loses ₹100 crore monthly:Phones and WhatsApp hacked without clicking links or sharing OTPs; what is this new scam?
stories.summary: Suppose your phone is kept in your pocket. You have neither clicked on any unknown link, nor shared an OTP with anyone, nor answered any suspicious call. Yet, suddenly calls start coming in from friends and relatives asking, "Brother, why did you need money?" Surprised, you open WhatsApp, but neither is any message sent there nor is any chat visible. This is not a film story, but the new face of rapidly spreading cybercrime in UP. According to the Ministry of Home Affairs, more than 1.85 lakh complaints of cyber fraud were registered in UP from January to June this year. This is the highest in the country. Meanwhile, an average of more than ₹100 crore in cyber fraud is taking place every month in the state. How do phones and WhatsApp get hacked after all without clicking a link or sharing an OTP? The hacker sends messages from your own number and you don't even get a hint, why does this happen? We will know today in UP Explainer… Question 1: How does a phone get hacked without clicking on a link or without sharing an OTP? Answer: This type of cyber fraud is called a zero-click attack. This method is extremely expensive and high-tech. In this, the hacker exploits a flaw in the phone's software simply by sending a missed call or a special kind of data file, and the phone gets hacked without clicking anything at all. Question 2: The notifications and messages of the WhatsApp chats that the hacker does are not visible on the user's phone, how does this happen? Answer: According to UP Police's Cyber Security Advisor Rahul Mishra, in such cases, hackers do this through WhatsApp's 'Linked Devices' feature and chat settings. When WhatsApp gets connected to the hacker's computer or another phone, they can chat with anyone in our contact list without leaving any evidence in our phone. Understand in simple language how this entire work happens behind the scenes… Not getting notifications on the phone: When the hacker messages someone from their computer, they immediately mute the notifications of that chat. Due to this, when a reply comes from the other side, its notification does not appear on the main phone. Sent messages not being visible: A speciality of WhatsApp is that if the same account is running in two places (on your phone and on the hacker's computer), a message deleted from one place gets removed from the other place as well. As soon as the hacker sends a message asking for money to one of our acquaintances and reads their reply, they immediately do 'Delete for me' on those messages from their computer. Since both devices are connected to the internet, as soon as the hacker deletes it, that message immediately disappears from our phone as well. Question 3: How to know if the phone has been hacked? Answer: When a hacker steals data from the phone, pressure is put on the phone's system. Due to this, some signs start appearing… Question 4: What to do first if the phone or WhatsApp gets hacked? Answer: If your phone or WhatsApp gets hacked, without panicking, first disconnect the hacker's connection. First, turn off your phone's mobile data and Wi-Fi or put the phone on Aeroplane mode. This will break the hacker's control over the phone. Secure bank accounts and email: Call the bank's customer care or temporarily block net banking and UPI from another safe phone. Immediately change the passwords of your main email, bank apps, and social media from another safe phone or computer. Alert friends and family: Immediately call or message your family, friends, and office colleagues to inform them that your WhatsApp or phone has been hacked. Tell them not to trust any message asking for money or any unknown link coming from your number. Do a factory reset: If the entire phone has been hacked, take a backup of your important photos and numbers and do a factory reset (complete format) of the phone. This is the surest way to completely remove any virus hidden in the phone. File a complaint with Cyber Crime: If money has been deducted from your bank account or your name is being misused, immediately call the National Cyber Helpline number 1930. You can also register a complaint on the website cybercrime.gov.in. Question 5: What precautions should be taken so that the phone does not get hacked? Answer: For this, turning on some essential security settings of the phone is enough. Most cyber-attacks happen due to haste or opening unknown files. 1. Avoid unknown links and files Never open any unknown links for free recharge, government schemes, electricity bills, bank KYC, or lottery coming on WhatsApp or SMS. Never install any .apk file coming on WhatsApp in the name of a wedding card, traffic challan, or bank statement. Always download apps only from the Google Play Store or Apple App Store. 2. Adjust necessary settings Go to WhatsApp's Settings > Storage and data and turn off the auto-download of photos, videos, and documents. As soon as an update for the phone or any app arrives, install it immediately. Turn off the phone and turn it back on (restart) every one or two days. This automatically eliminates viruses hidden in the phone's temporary memory. 3. Internet and charging safety Never use bank apps or UPI via free Wi-Fi at railway stations, hotels, or cafes. Instead of charging the phone by plugging the data cable directly into a charging point, always use your own charger's adapter (plug).

stories.title: SP asks Congress to finalise seat-sharing in three days:Sets 23–25 November deadline; meeting on UP elections had been postponed
stories.summary: For the Uttar Pradesh elections, the Samajwadi Party has offered to finalise seat-sharing with the Congress within three days. The party has proposed meetings in Delhi on 23, 24 and 25 November for seat-sharing. SP MP Rajeev Rai said that holding continuous meetings instead of meeting repeatedly would save time. In fact, a meeting of SP and Congress leaders was scheduled to be held in Delhi on 17 November. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav had reached Delhi on Monday, but the meeting was suddenly postponed. Formal talks on seat-sharing had taken place between Akhilesh and the Congress's top leadership. It had emerged that three-member committees from both parties would hold discussions. Congress had sought 181 seats in the Uttar Pradesh elections The Congress held a party meeting at Mallikarjun Kharge's residence in Delhi on Monday. Even before talks on seat-sharing with the Samajwadi Party began, it staked a claim to 181 seats. According to sources, Akhilesh Yadav also wants to deliberate with his leaders and formulate a strategy before the meeting. After the meeting was postponed, Samajwadi Party MLA Ravidas Mehrotra said, "Talks are underway between the national presidents of the Samajwadi Party and the Congress. There will definitely be an alliance. A Samajwadi Party wave is sweeping Uttar Pradesh. Our party is going to form the government on its own. The people have decided that they want change. They want Akhilesh Yadav to become chief minister." Read the 3 reasons why the Samajwadi Party-Congress meeting was postponed 1. Congress's demand for 181 seats makes the SP uncomfortable: The Congress has handed the SP a list of 181 seats out of Uttar Pradesh's 403 seats. The SP is not in favour of giving such a large number of seats. Akhilesh has already said that, in the alliance, a seat should go to the party whose candidate is in a position to win. 2. Unease grows after seat list is made public Unease is also being seen between the two parties after details of the Congress's demand for 181 seats became public. Tensions between the parties have increased after the numbers and claims emerged even before discussions on seat-sharing began within the alliance. 3. SP insists on forming a coordination committee before talks The SP says a coordination committee will be formed for the talks. Formal discussions on the seats will take place after that. Akhilesh is likely to authorise Prof. Ram Gopal Yadav and MP Rajeev Rai to hold the discussions. The Congress has also formed a five-member committee on its side. In such a situation, both parties first want to decide the framework for the talks.

stories.title: BJP says 'no one's future will be ruined by UGC':Central leadership admits mistake in framing rules at Mathura meeting
stories.summary: The BJP has started preparing its strategy for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. At a two-day meeting in Mathura, the party decided to focus mainly on young people and women. It also discussed ways to use social media and short videos to remind new voters of incidents during the Samajwadi Party (SP) government. The meeting was held on November 17 at the Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Research Centre in Farah, Mathura. The issue of the University Grants Commission's (UGC) new regulations also came up during the meeting. BJP leaders and workers raised concerns over the rules. The central leadership said the government had accepted that there were some mistakes in drafting the regulations and that these would be corrected. The leadership assured those present that no law or rule would be implemented if it harmed anyone's future or treated any section unfairly. The matter is currently pending before the Supreme Court. The leadership said the government would take the necessary steps through the legal process and ensure that the interests of all sections were protected. Why is the BJP focusing on young people and women? According to BJP leaders who attended the meeting, many young people who will vote for the first or second time in 2027 were very young during the SP government before 2017. They have seen BJP governments at the Centre since 2014 and in Uttar Pradesh since 2017. The party believes these voters should also know about the law and order situation, recruitment controversies, the Jawaharbaug incident and issues related to women's safety during the earlier government. The BJP plans to use social media reels and other online content to reach these voters. Reels on old statements: The party plans to use videos of statements made by SP leaders during the Ram temple movement. BJP leaders said SP chief Akhilesh Yadav is now visiting the Ram temple, while Mulayam Singh Yadav, Ram Gopal Yadav and Shivpal Yadav had made different statements on the issue in the past. Targeting Dalit voters: The party also plans to highlight an old statement by SP leader Azam Khan about Dr BR Ambedkar. BJP leaders want to use it to question the SP's claims of supporting Dalits and backward classes. Only 25% of young people receiving tablets were voters Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath shared an important figure related to voter registration during the meeting. He said tablets had been distributed in Lucknow to young people above the age of 18 under the Swami Vivekananda Student Empowerment Scheme. When they were asked how many were registered voters, only 25% raised their hands. Yogi directed party office-bearers to ensure that all eligible young people were registered as voters. He also asked them to compare the voter lists prepared for panchayat elections with the Assembly voter list so that no eligible voter was left out. BJP leadership rejects rumours about candidates and leadership BJP national president Nitin Nabin said the party organisation was its top priority. He also made it clear that there was no crisis over the leadership or government in Uttar Pradesh. He said people had faith in the work of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. 209-candidate list called misleading: Nitin Nabin and Yogi Adityanath rejected a list of 209 candidates that was circulating on social media. They asked party workers not to believe such rumours and said tickets would be decided through the party's official process. Every worker will get responsibility: Nitin Nabin said no party worker should stay at home during the election campaign. Everyone would be given a responsibility. State president Pankaj Chaudhary began the second day of the meeting with the slogan, "Radhe-Radhe, make the lotus bloom". He said no opposition party, including the SP, BSP, Congress, Azad Samaj Party and AIMIM, would succeed in Uttar Pradesh. 'Nationalism' to counter caste politics Nitin Nabin told party workers that opposition parties were trying to divide society on caste lines. He said the BJP should bring young people and women together around the issue of nationalism instead. He said the SP, BSP, Congress and third front were all political rivals and the party would have to adopt a strong campaign against them. BJP leaders suggest slogans for election campaign The meeting also discussed slogans to give the BJP's election campaign more momentum. Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak suggested around a dozen slogans. 'Uttar Pradesh will respond' emerged as the most prominent one. MLC Santosh Singh and Parliamentary Affairs Minister Suresh Khanna also suggested slogans. The party will now form a special team of former and current office-bearers. The team will prepare a plan to take the campaign issues and messages to the public.

stories.summary: At the Benti Raj Bhavan of Raja Bhaiya, the MLA from Kunda in Pratapgarh, Pandit Dhirendra Krishna Shastri delivered a Shriram Katha. During the event, he said that he had apologised so that his Hindu brothers would not fight among themselves. He would go to Vrindavan very soon. "Let's head towards Mathura and put in one more push." A large number of MPs, MLAs and ministers arrived to hear Dhirendra Shastri's katha. Around 80,000 people remained inside the tent, while 20,000 listened to the katha from outside. Former MP Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, who had arrived to hear his katha, said from the stage, "Raja Bhaiya, you had influence before, you have it today and you will continue to have it in the future." Before this, Dhirendra Shastri had travelled to Gonda to attend Rajan Maharaj's katha. After staying there for around two hours, he returned to Kunda at 2:45 p.m. on Tuesday afternoon. During this time, he took a jibe at Akhilesh Yadav without naming him. He said- Earlier, when yajnas were held, demons and ogres would throw in bones. Now people post things online-the only difference is that. In fact, on 5 November 2026, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav had demanded that Dhirendra Shastri's religious discourses scheduled in Pratapgarh, Gonda, Jhansi, Lucknow and Agra be cancelled.

stories.title: Teenager dies after being hit by car:Family protests as body remains missing, accuses police of assault
stories.summary: A 17-year-old boy died after being hit by a car in Barbirwa, Krishna Nagar, Lucknow, on Monday night. A dispute broke out when the body reached home after the post-mortem on Tuesday evening. The family alleged that instead of handing over the body to them, the police took it into custody. They also allegedly assaulted the deceased's elder brother. Angered by this, the family began protesting against the police. Police reached the spot after being informed and pacified them by assuring them of action. Ram Ghulam, originally from Mardan Kheda Purwa in Unnao, lives with his wife, Kishan Kumari, and six sons on the pavement in front of the Mansarovar LDA Market in Baravirwa, Krishna Nagar. His youngest son, Ankush (17), was hit at around 9:30 p.m. on Monday by an unidentified car coming from Kanpur Road. After the accident, the driver fled towards Pakri Bridge. Police reached the spot and took the injured Ankush to Lokbandhu Hospital, where doctors declared him dead. The police sent the body for a post-mortem. Police oppose preparations to place body at the crossroads After the body reached the family home following the post-mortem on Tuesday evening, the family members began demanding that it be handed over to them. The police allegedly took the body into their custody instead of handing it over to them. The police were also accused of assaulting Mukesh, the deceased's elder brother, during the incident. The family members and people from their community then became agitated and began protesting against the police. Krishnanagar Inspector-in-Charge PK Singh said that before the accident, Ankush had been quarrelling with a companion while under the influence of alcohol. During this, he was hit by a car and died. The family was preparing to place his body at the crossroads. They were stopped from doing so, following which a commotion broke out. The family has now taken the body to their ancestral village. A case will be registered and action will be taken once a complaint is received.

stories.title: Man keeps firing gun as people pelt him with stones:Neither bullets nor stones hit anyone; video of neighbours' clash in Lucknow
stories.summary: A fierce fight broke out in a neighbourhood in Lucknow's Sarojininagar on Tuesday morning. During the clash, some people pelted their neighbour with bricks and stones. The neighbour then pulled out a country-made pistol and fired several rounds. A woman recorded the entire incident on video. The full video is 3 minutes and 10 seconds long. Watching it will leave you breathless. In the end, no one was injured in the neighbourhood fight. The man who fired the pistol was not hit by any stones, and none of those who pelted him with stones was hit by a bullet. The police have detained the man who opened fire with the country-made pistol. See the entire fight in three pictures... Shopkeeper opens fire at hotel manager's wife The incident took place in Rustam Vihar Colony. It happened at around 7:30 a.m. on Tuesday. Mohammad Ikhlaq of the colony is a manager at a hotel near the Secretariat. In his complaint to the police, he said that Mohammad Ali, who runs a grocery shop in the neighbourhood, opened fire at his wife, Shazia. People living nearby gathered after hearing the gunfire. The incident occurred when he was returning home after dropping the children at school. His wife came outside to give him his bag. At that point, their neighbour, Mohammad Ali, threatened to throw acid on Shazia's face over an old dispute. The argument escalated, and he brought out a country-made pistol. He fired twice, but no one was hit either time It is alleged that as the dispute escalated, Mohammad Ali brought a country-made pistol from his house and pointed it at Shazia. The two sides exchanged abuses. He then opened fire, but no one was hit. After the firing, he went inside the house. Angry over this, people from Ikhlaq's side threw bricks and stones at Mohammed Ali's gate. He came outside again and opened fire at them. No one was hit by a bullet the second time either. He pointed a country-made pistol at neighbours who came to calm the situation Hearing the sound of gunfire, local residents reached the spot and began trying to calm both sides. Mohammed Ali allegedly abused the neighbours and pointed a country-made pistol at them as well. When people ran, he went inside the house. He then threw bricks and stones from the roof and tried to open fire. Local residents informed the police. The police have taken the accused into custody and are investigating the case.

stories.title: Gorakhpur Police destroy 76.46 kg of ganja worth ₹38.23 lakh:Contraband seized in 11 separate cases
stories.summary: Police in Gorakhpur destroyed illegal cannabis worth ₹38.23 lakh on Tuesday under 'Operation Dahan'. Following a court order, 76.460 kg of cannabis linked to 11 cases registered at seven different police stations in the district was burnt to ashes in a high-capacity incinerator. The action was completed transparently under the supervision of senior police officers. Property from 11 cases at these seven police stations destroyed The narcotics destroyed were linked to a total of 11 cases registered at Khajni, AIIMS, Belipar, Sahjanwa, Khorabar, Gola and Gorakhnath police stations in the district. After receiving legal permission from the court, police began the process of destroying the cannabis that had been stored in the malkhanas of these police stations for a long time. Burnt in a high-capacity incinerator Environmental and safety regulations were fully observed while destroying the narcotics. A high-capacity incinerator at A.V. Bio Medical Waste Services, located in Sector 15A of GIDA, was used for the purpose. This ensured that toxic smoke did not spread outside and that the material was destroyed safely. Action completed before the Drug Disposal Committee The entire process was completed in the presence of the 'Drug Disposal Committee' formed by the government. SP Crime, CO Traffic, officer in charge of the Narcotics Cell and specialist police personnel from all seven police stations were present. Police officials said the campaign would continue to ensure the safe disposal of narcotics seized and stored at police stations.

stories.title: Activist calls Agra ACP ‘Behen Ji’, officer loses her temper:Argument erupts after police stop Parshuram Dal workers’ rally; she says, ‘I am not Behen Ji’
stories.summary: A video of an argument between Sadar ACP Ameesha and Parshuram Dal activists in Agra has gone viral on social media. Police stopped the activists on their way as they were taking out a rally to protest the UGC Bill. During the incident, an activist addressed the ACP as "sister", which angered her. She said, "I am not sister." The activist replied, "We will call you sister; this is our Indian culture." Now read the full story On Sunday, 15 November, the Parshuram Dal was holding a rally in Agra to protest the UGC Bill. The police stopped the rally on the way. An argument then broke out between Parshuram Dal leaders and police personnel. The police cited the enforcement of Section 163 to stop the rally. The Parshuram Dal activists questioned how permission had been granted to hold a Dalit conference at the GIC ground when Section 163 was in force. 'You Can Challenge It in Court' During the dispute, Sadar ACP Amisha told the activists that they could challenge the matter in court. Amid the exchange, one activist told the ACP, "Please listen, sister." The ACP expressed her displeasure and said, "I am not your sister." The activist replied, "We will call you sister. It is part of our Indian culture. We call people sister. All Indians are our brothers and sisters." The argument between the two sides continued for quite some time during the exchange. Who is ACP Amisha Singh Amisha Singh is originally from Lucknow and was born on 12 May 1997. Her father, Vinod Kumar Singh, has also served as an IPS officer in the Uttar Pradesh Police. Her father had retired. She completed her early education in Lucknow and her graduation and postgraduation (BA and MA) at Delhi University. She secured 18th rank in the UPPSC (UPPSC) 2022 examination and was selected as a DSP. Her first posting as an ACP was in Agra. She made headlines after solving Agra's high-profile 'bathroom murder case', in which a wife killed her husband and buried his body in the bathroom.

stories.title: Mother saves daughter from leopard’s jaws in Bahraich:Big cat ripped mosquito net and tried to flee with child
stories.summary: In Bahraich, a mother fought a leopard to rescue her six-year-old daughter from its jaws. The leopard tore through the mosquito net and seized the girl while she was sleeping inside the house. It began dragging her away with her jaws clamped in its mouth. The girl then called out to her mother. As soon as she heard her daughter's screams, the mother confronted the leopard without losing a moment. While the leopard pulled the girl towards itself with her jaws clamped in its mouth, the mother used all her strength to free her. She did not give up. Eventually, she pulled her daughter into her arms and rescued her from the leopard's clutches. The girl was injured in the struggle. Hearing the commotion, people from the surrounding area also reached the spot. When it saw people approaching, the leopard fled towards the forest. The injured girl has been admitted to a medical college, where she is undergoing treatment. The incident took place in the Sujauli police station area, around 80 kilometres from the district headquarters. A leopard entered the house when the mother got up to charge her mobile phone Tepara village in the Sujauli police station area is adjacent to the forest. Rajesh Chauhan (35) lives there with his family. His family comprises his wife, Bindrawati (33), two daughters, Anshika (11) and Divya (6), and a son. At night, both daughters slept with their mother on the same charpoy under a mosquito net. At around 5 a.m., Bindrawati got up to feed the buffalo. Divya woke up with her. Divya asked her mother to put her mobile phone on charge. As her mother turned to plug in the phone, a leopard entered the house from behind. It tore through the mosquito net and clamped Divya in its jaws. It then dragged the child to the veranda. When Divya called out to her mother, Bindrawati turned around. Seeing her daughter caught in the leopard's jaws, she confronted it to rescue her. She pulled the child towards herself with all her strength. Hearing the commotion, her husband Rajesh and neighbours also reached the spot. When people raised an alarm, the leopard released the child and fled towards the forest. Mother said she ran after hearing her daughter's cries Bindrawati said, "The girl was sleeping beside me. I woke up in the morning to feed the buffalo. The buffalo was tethered outside. Just then, my daughter said, 'Mummy, put the mobile phone on charge.' I began charging the phone when the girl screamed, 'Mummy... Mummy, the leopard has caught me.' I ran over and saw the leopard pulling the girl towards itself. I grabbed the girl and began pulling her towards me." The leopard had dragged her up to the veranda Bindravati said, "The leopard dragged the girl a short distance to the veranda. I held the girl in my arms, pulled her towards me with all my strength and freed her from its grip. Blood had spread across the girl's entire body. We took her to Sujauli, where she received stitches. After that, we were told to take her to the Mihinpurwa block. From there, the girl was sent here." Injuries to hand, abdomen and neck Divya suffered injuries to her neck, hands and abdomen in the leopard attack. Her mother was unharmed. The family first took the injured girl to the nearest CHC. When her condition did not improve, doctors referred her to Bahraich Medical College. Divya is currently receiving treatment at the medical college. Emergency Medical Officer (EMO) Dr Ashish Verma said, "The girl has suffered a serious injury to her neck. She also has injuries on other parts of her body. She has been admitted to the emergency ward and is receiving treatment." Forest department provides ₹5,000 aid and sets up a cage in the area DFO Apoorva Dixit said that as soon as the Forest Department was informed of the incident, a team reached the spot and conducted an investigation. Footprints found around the scene confirmed that they belonged to a leopard. The victim's family was immediately given financial assistance of ₹5,000. The Forest Department has also installed a cage in the area. It has appealed to villagers to remain alert at night and take precautions around their homes. The entire area is adjacent to the forest. Leopards are frequently seen here.

stories.title: Gorakhpur to get second e-bus charging station:Facility to charge 4 buses at once as city prepares to deploy 150 new AC buses
stories.summary: Preparations are underway to improve the operation of electric city buses in Gorakhpur, alongside plans to increase their fleet. The city's second electric bus charging station will be built at the city bus depot in Chargawan. The project will cost ₹4.64 crore and cover an area of around 2,000 square metres. The facility will be equipped to charge four electric buses simultaneously. To benefit buses operating in northern Gorakhpur The new facility, coming up after the first charging station at Mahesra, will be particularly useful for buses operating in northern Gorakhpur and nearby areas. Currently, all electric buses operating in the city depend on the Mahesra depot for charging. Buses serving the northern parts of the city also have to travel to Mahesra, spending considerable time on the road. The Chargawan station will eliminate the need for these long journeys for charging. This is expected to save operational time and allow buses to make more trips. Tender issued, scheduled to open on November 17 CD.S.-42 has been assigned responsibility for constructing the charging station and has issued a tender for the work. According to the schedule, the tender will be opened on November 17. The contractual process will then be completed with the selected agency, after which construction will begin. Preparations underway to expand electric bus services Preparations are underway to introduce 150 new air-conditioned electric city buses to strengthen public transport in Gorakhpur. With the expansion of the fleet, the city will also need additional charging infrastructure. At present, Mahesara has the city's only electric bus charging station. It could face increasing pressure as more buses are added in the coming months. To address this, a second charging station is planned at Chargawan. Depots and other essential facilities are also being expanded to support the new buses. The proposed station at Chargawan will allow buses operating in northern Gorakhpur to charge locally, reducing their dependence on the Mahesara depot. More trips for buses, shorter waits for passengers Currently, electric buses operating on routes in northern Gorakhpur and nearby areas have to travel to Mahesara for charging. This takes them away from their designated routes and requires them to cover additional distance. They also take time to return to their routes after charging, affecting bus operations. The new station at Chargawan is expected to address this problem by allowing buses to charge closer to their operating areas and resume services sooner. This will help increase the number of trips they can make. Passengers are also expected to benefit from shorter waiting times, particularly in northern areas of Gorakhpur that rely on city buses for public transport. Station to charge four buses at a time The proposed charging station will cover around 2,000 square metres and will have the capacity to charge four electric buses simultaneously. The project is estimated to cost ₹4.64 crore and is expected to support the expansion of electric bus services. With preparations underway to introduce 150 new air-conditioned buses, the station will strengthen the city's charging infrastructure. The expansion of electric bus services is also expected to help reduce pollution and improve public transport facilities for passengers.

stories.title: Panchayat representatives gherao minister’s residence in Lucknow:Throw sweets boxes and jostle with police personnel
stories.summary: The Panchayat Adhikar Sangh staged a protest in Lucknow on Tuesday (17 Nov), demanding that panchayat elections be held soon in Uttar Pradesh. Gram pradhans, area panchayat members, district panchayat members and other panchayat representatives from across the state surrounded the residence of Panchayati Raj Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar. They raised slogans loudly during the protest. Angry protesters also threw boxes of sweets at the minister's residence. When the police tried to stop them, pushing and heated exchanges broke out. The police later detained the protesters and sent them to Eco Garden. The protesters raised slogans such as "No government in the Assembly if there is no government in the villages" and "Hold the panchayat elections soon". They said that the election date had not been announced even though the panchayats' terms had ended. This was affecting development work in the villages and the resolution of local problems. See three pictures... Pradhans' term ended on 26 May Panchayat representative Anand Kumar said that the term of the village pradhans ended on 26 May. The government then extended their term by six months. That period is also set to end soon. Despite this, the date for the panchayat elections has not been announced. He said Part IX, Articles 243-E and 243-K of the Constitution of India provide for regular and timely elections to panchayats. Despite this, the situation regarding the elections has not been clarified. Around 13 crore rural residents and 8 lakh potential candidates are waiting for the election date. He warned that the agitation would be intensified if the government did not provide a written assurance. The panchayat representatives said that the three-tier panchayat elections should be held in the state as soon as possible. Opposition to extending the term again The protesters also expressed anger over the possibility that the government might extend the term of the panchayats again. They said a six-month extension had already been granted. They warned that any further attempt to extend the term would be opposed. They said holding panchayat elections on time was part of the democratic system. Delays in the elections were affecting the functioning of the village governments. Panchayat representatives described this as an ignoring of their democratic rights and demanded that the elections be held soon. Anger also expressed over minister's statement The protesters also expressed anger at Panchayati Raj Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar. They alleged that despite staging continuous protests since 12 June, they had received only assurances. Neither had the election date been announced nor had their problems been resolved. Referring to a statement by the minister, the protesters said that nearly eight lakh candidates had begun preparing for the election, but no clear information was now being provided about it. They said their protest would continue until the election date was announced.

stories.title: UP sees an increase of 18.84 lakh voters after SIR:Draft electoral roll released, number of women voters rises more significantly
stories.summary: Voter numbers in Uttar Pradesh have increased by 18,84,113 following the Special Intensive Revision (SIR). Addressing a press conference in Lucknow on Tuesday, Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) Navdeep Rinwa said that the draft electoral rolls for all 403 Assembly constituencies across the state's 75 districts are being published today. “The names of 7,87,449 male and 10,96,828 female voters have been added to the electoral rolls following the SIR”, he added. Meetings with political parties to be held in 75 districts Rinwa said that after the draft electoral rolls are released, all district election officers will hold meetings with representatives of recognised national and state-level political parties. They will be provided with the electoral rolls and informed about the revision process. The public will also be able to view the electoral rolls on the websites of their respective district election officers. BLOs to verify electoral rolls until 20 November The draft electoral roll will be available with the Booth-Level Officers (BLOs) deployed at 1,73,730 polling stations across the state. From 17 to 20 November, the BLOs will identify errors in the roll through a tabletop exercise and take further action as per the rules. The CEO has appealed to political parties to appoint Booth-Level Agents (BLAs) at every polling station so that their participation in the revision of the electoral roll can be ensured. He said the objective of the Special Summary Revision-2027 is to update the electoral roll, rectify errors and include the names of all eligible citizens in it.

stories.title: Woman sub-inspector found dead in bathroom in Noida:She was posted at Jarcha police station; heart attack suspected
stories.summary: A 27-year-old woman sub-inspector was found dead in the bathroom of her government accommodation in Greater Noida. When she did not answer her phone on Tuesday (17 Nov) morning, her father asked a fellow woman sub-inspector to check on her. The colleague knocked on the door several times but received no response. She then called the police from the station. When police personnel broke open the door, they found the sub-inspector dead inside. Sub-inspector was posted at Jarcha police station Rashmi Gautam, a native of Kanpur, had no visible injury marks on her body. Police suspect she may have died of a heart attack, though the exact cause is yet to be established. She was a 2023-batch sub-inspector posted at Jarcha police station. Sub-inspector lived alone, father called her every morning Rashmi lived alone in government accommodation on the premises of Jarcha police station. Her father is a head constable in the fire department in Kanpur Dehat. According to police, he called her every morning at around 7 am to check on her. He called her several times on Tuesday (17 Nov) morning as well, but she did not answer. Suspecting something was wrong, he asked a fellow woman sub-inspector to visit her accommodation. He also informed Jarcha police station in-charge Kailash Nath. Post-mortem report to establish cause of death When police broke open the door latch and entered the accommodation, they found Rashmi lying unconscious in the bathroom. She was rushed to hospital, where doctors declared her dead. Station in-charge Kailash Nath said the family had been informed about the incident. The body had been sent for a post-mortem, and the exact cause of death would be established once the report was received.
