stories.title: LJP announces plans to contest UP Assembly elections:Chirag Paswan says party will first strengthen organisation and expand its outreach across households
stories.summary: The Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) will contest the upcoming Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. Party national president Chirag Paswan arrived in Lucknow on Tuesday (17 Nov) and confirmed that the decision to enter the electoral contest had been finalised. However, the party has not yet decided whether it will contest independently or join an alliance. With time still left before the elections, its immediate focus is on strengthening its organisational base across the state. Party aims to take its ideology and policies to every household Chirag Paswan said the party was working to expand its organisation in Uttar Pradesh. Along with strengthening its workers, efforts were underway to take the party's ideology and policies to every household. He said his priority at present was to strengthen the organisation and bring as many people as possible into the party. Alliance decision to be taken closer to elections On the possibility of an alliance, Paswan said no decision had been taken so far. Since the elections were still some time away, the party would not rush into any decision. He said the alliance strategy would be decided closer to the elections, taking into account the prevailing political circumstances. For now, the party will focus on expanding its organisation and increasing its support base across Uttar Pradesh.

stories.title: KGMU seniors force juniors to salute them:Students bow their heads, repeatedly say, ‘Pranam Mahoday Ji’; security guards record videos
stories.summary: The scene outside the Kalam Centre at King George's Medical University (KGMU) around 1.30 pm on Monday was striking. First-year MBBS students stood in a queue with their heads bowed. Whenever a senior student walked past, they would loudly greet them, saying, "Greetings, sir." Female students in the queue also greeted senior female students with "Greetings, ma'am". Several security guards were present nearby, with some recording videos on their mobile phones. Senior students passing the queue were seen reprimanding juniors and issuing instructions. The first-year students remained standing with their heads bowed, visibly anxious. None appeared willing to leave the queue or raise an objection. First-year students pressured to show deference to seniors New students are reportedly made to stand together in groups and bow whenever they pass in front of senior students. Those who object to the practice are scolded and intimidated. The constant pressure has left the first-year students frightened. They fear that seniors may harass them further if they lodge a complaint, making them hesitant to speak openly about their concerns. Ragging allegations surface despite security deployment and CCTV cameras The alleged activities reportedly continued even with security personnel deployed around the Kalam Centre and CCTV cameras installed on the premises. The incident was also captured in the camera footage recorded that afternoon. However, no effective intervention by the officials responsible has come to light so far. The silence of the first-year students and the fear visible on their faces have raised questions about the campus security arrangements and the action taken to prevent such incidents.

stories.title: Azam Khan gets interim bail from Allahabad HC:Court says arresting him at the prison gate after release was malicious
stories.summary: Senior Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan has received major relief from the Allahabad High Court. A division bench of the High Court granted him interim bail in a money laundering case filed by the Enforcement Directorate (ED). The court observed that, prima facie, the mandatory provisions of Article 22(1) of the Constitution and Section 19 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) were not strictly followed during Azam Khan's arrest. The court has directed that Azam Khan be released on a personal bond and two sureties of the like amount. He will be required to furnish the bail bond to the satisfaction of the Chief Judicial Magistrate (CJM) of Ghaziabad. The next hearing of the case is scheduled for December 10.

stories.title: BJP's new slogan in UP- 'Radhe Radhe, Kamal Khila De':MP calls it Mathura brainstorming meet's message; focus shifts to Krishna Janmabhoomi after Ayodhya
stories.summary: The BJP’s two-day Chintan Baithak (brainstorming session) in Mathura concluded at 4 PM on Tuesday. During the meeting, leaders deliberated on strategies to form the government in Uttar Pradesh for a third consecutive term. Following the session, Rajya Sabha MP Prakash Pal stated that the core message of the Mathura meeting is: "Radhe-Radhe, Kamal Khila De (make the lotus bloom)." Earlier, BJP National President Nitin Nabin also attended the meeting. Alongside reviewing election preparations, he assessed the performance reports of the MLAs. Statements from BJP leaders emerging from the meeting signalled the party's shift in focus toward Mathura after Ayodhya. Deputy CM Keshav Maurya remarked, "Ayodhya is ours now, next is Mathura's turn. If Akhilesh Yadav is truly a devotee of Lord Krishna, he should prepare to come to Mathura as a karsevak." On the first day of the session on Monday, discussions had also lasted for nearly seven hours, attended by around 50 senior party leaders, including Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and both Deputy Chief Ministers.

stories.title: Dense fog engulfs UP, temperatures below 15°C in 10 cities:Visibility drops to 20 metres in Varanasi, two-day alert issued
stories.summary: Cold conditions have intensified across Uttar Pradesh, with chilly weather being felt during the mornings and evenings. Fog covered Varanasi, Mirzapur, Deoria, Gorakhpur and Rampur on Tuesday morning. Visibility in Varanasi dropped so sharply that it was difficult to see beyond 20 metres on the roads. The Meteorological Department said the impact of cold north-westerly winds had increased after the passage of a fresh western disturbance. Temperatures have fallen below 15°C in 10 cities across the state. Dense fog is expected to continue over the next two to three days, while temperatures may drop by another 2-4°C. Severe cold likely across UP within a week Atul Kumar Singh, a meteorologist in Lucknow, said north-westerly winds were now gaining strength. He said severe cold conditions were likely to set in across the state within a week. People would also feel the chill during the daytime, with temperatures likely to reach normal or below-normal levels. It is a score that indicates the quality of the air and helps us understand whether the air around us is clean or polluted. The levels of pollutants present in the air are measured in the AQI. The higher the AQI, the more hazardous the air is considered to be, and the greater the health risk. Understand it through the graphic below: How does poor AQI affect our health? When the AQI is poor, pollutants such as PM2.5, PM10, nitrogen dioxide, sulphur dioxide and ozone in the air reach deep into our lungs. These particles spread throughout the body through the bloodstream. They can cause several types of health problems, ranging from immediate issues to long-term conditions. stories.title: Woman found with throat slit in hotel, man found hanging:Hotel KJ owned by Varanasi BJP MLA's relative; body found in bathroom
stories.summary: A young woman was murdered by having her throat slit in a room at Hotel KJ International on Varanasi Airport Road, while the body of her sister's brother-in-law, who had been staying in the room, was found hanging from a noose. The young woman was found inside the bathroom with her throat slit and her body covered in blood. There were marks of assault on her face and body, and hair was scattered around the room. The circumstances made it clear that an argument had taken place in the room before the murder. However, the deceased man, who worked at BLW, and the woman, a resident of Baragaon, were relatives. There was a commotion after the bodies were found in the locked room on Monday night. The Baragaon police promptly reached the spot and gathered information about the bodies. After identifying the man and woman staying at the hotel, their family members were called and the door was broken open. The police examined the CCTV footage. The police are describing the case as the woman's murder and the man's suicide. Here is the full sequence of events Jai Vikas, son of Raj Prakash Kesari, a 20-year-old resident of BLW in Varanasi's Manduadih police station area, reached Basni Baragaon, his brother's in-laws' home, from where he left with his sister-in-law's sister, Priya Kesari, daughter of Nandlal Kesari, aged 24. The two reached the KJ International Hotel on Airport Road on a motorcycle and booked a room for 16 November. They provided their Aadhaar details and entered their names and addresses in the hotel's entry register. Passing his sister-in-law's sister off as his sister-in-law, the two went to their room and ordered coffee. After telling room service that they were going out, the two began arguing over something in the room. When Jai Vikas brought up the matter of the young woman's marriage being fixed, Priya denied it. After the two exchanged heated words, marriage was discussed while referring to the family. Later, when the hotel staff called them for dinner at night, there was no response. They went to the door and knocked, and also called their mobile numbers, but no one answered the phone inside. Amid fears that something untoward had happened, the hotel employees informed the manager and owner. They then told the Badagaon police that the two appeared to be in a suspicious condition inside the room. Police called the relatives, then broke down the door Officers reached the spot with police personnel immediately after receiving information on the night of 16 November that two people had been found dead at KJ International Hotel in Babatpur. Both families were informed and called to the spot, and a forensic team was also summoned. In the presence of the families, the hotel room door was broken open. Both people were found dead inside. There was a mark on the young woman's neck indicating a knife attack, while the young man's body was found hanging from a noose. After the door was broken open, DCP Gomti Neetu Kadyan and ADCP went inside and examined the circumstances. The officers initially suspected suicide, although the police team is investigating the matter. Baragaon police took both bodies into custody, after which the forensic team was called. The team collected evidence, including the fingerprints of both people and other fingerprints from the room. It may be noted that KJ International Hotel is owned by a relative of a BJP MLA. Complaints of undesirable activities at the hotel had reached the administration several times in the past as well, but no action was taken due to pressure from those in power. Young man hanged himself after killing woman: DCP Deputy Commissioner of Police, Gomti Zone, Neetu Kadyan, said the investigation revealed that the young man and woman were related. The man was the younger brother of the woman's sister's husband. Prima facie, it appears that the man killed the woman and then hanged himself. The hotel's entry register contained entries for Jai Vikas, son of Jai Prakash Kesari, a resident of Bhikharipur, DLW, Manduadih police station, Varanasi, aged around 20, and Priya Kesari, daughter of Nandlal Kesari, a resident of Basni, Baragaon police station, Varanasi, aged around 23. The site is being inspected and the necessary evidence is being collected. Both bodies have been taken into custody and sent for the preparation of inquest reports and post-mortems. The Station House Officer of Badagaon has been given the necessary directions.

Killed woman, then raped her body 5 times:Says, 'Seeing her in a maxi dress triggered my intentions'
stories.summary: A man accused of murdering a couple in Kannauj allegedly raped the woman's body four to five times after killing her, according to his confession to the police. He told investigators that he became attracted to the woman after seeing her wearing a maxi dress while sweeping outside her house. Kannauj police arrested the accused, identified as Yogesh Singh Rajput alias Panga (25), on Sunday (November 15) after shooting him in both legs during an encounter. The couple were murdered on the night of November 4. The accused had allegedly committed a similar crime in 2022, when he killed a mother and daughter. The incident took place in the Gurusahai­ganj police station area, around 25 km from the district headquarters. Two bodies found, two-year-old daughter found crying beside father On the morning of November 5, the bodies of Sanjeev Katheria (36) and his wife Shikha (32) were found inside their quarters on the premises of an old Primary Health Centre (PHC). Their two-year-old daughter, Vanya, was found sitting beside her father's body and crying. The incident came to light when a relative reached the house. Sanjeev lived there with his wife, their seven-year-old son Pratyansh and their two-year-old daughter. He worked at a ticket vending machine at the railway station. Sanjeev's mother had worked as a midwife at the PHC. After her death, Shikha also helped at the hospital whenever required. The PHC was shifted to Tirwa Road three years ago because its building had deteriorated. Sanjeev's family was the only one still living on the old premises. Accused says he repeatedly watched woman secretly According to the police, CCTV footage showed a suspicious man, who was later identified as Yogesh, a resident of Bhojapur village in the Talgram area. In his alleged confession, Yogesh said he had recently been released from prison and was staying in Gurusahai­ganj. He frequently visited the railway station and the old PHC premises. He said he once saw Shikha sweeping while wearing a maxi dress. He claimed that he became attracted to her and started visiting the premises regularly to watch her secretly. Entered house through roof after waiting for couple to sleep Yogesh told the police that he visited the house two or three times on November 4 but found it locked. He continued waiting nearby until he saw the couple return. After waiting for them to fall asleep, he climbed onto the roof, cut through a plastic sheet and tarpaulin covering it, and jumped into the house. He was carrying a wooden stick. According to his account, Sanjeev and Shikha were sleeping on separate beds. When Sanjeev woke up after hearing a noise, Yogesh struck him on the head with the stick, killing him. Shikha woke up after hearing the commotion. Yogesh allegedly asked her to remain quiet, but she tried to call someone. He snatched her phone and disconnected the call before strangling her with her dupatta. Their daughter, who was sleeping beside her father, started crying. Yogesh allegedly picked her up and threw her down, killing her as well. He then allegedly raped Shikha's body four to five times. Took cash and ATM card, changed clothes before fleeing Yogesh told the police that he took Rs 5,000 and an ATM card from a purse before leaving the house. He escaped towards GT Road and then moved towards the railway tracks. He had allegedly hidden a change of clothes in nearby bushes beforehand. He discarded his bloodstained clothes and the wooden stick in an abandoned building, changed into the clothes he had hidden and fled. He further claimed that he was caught after stopping a man for money when he ran out of cash. The man raised an alarm, leading to his arrest. Had killed mother and daughter in 2022 Police said Yogesh had allegedly murdered a mother and daughter in Bhojapur village on November 29, 2022. He had entered their house intending to rape Anita (20). When her mother, Bhagwan Shri (50), woke up after hearing a noise and raised an alarm, he allegedly killed both women. Yogesh was arrested on December 2, 2022, and had remained in jail until his release about a month before the Kannauj murders. Police recover bloodstained clothes and weapon Superintendent of Police Vinod Kumar said a case had been registered on the complaint of Kotwali in-charge Dhyanendra Pratap Singh. The accused was taken to the district hospital for treatment after the police encounter. Following his discharge, he was taken to the crime scene, where the police recovered the bloodstained clothes and the wooden stick allegedly used in the murders. The police are completing the formalities to send him to jail.

stories.title: UP sanitation workers turn millionaires:Hired labourers on contract for ₹300; some own petrol pumps, others marriage halls
stories.summary: Several sanitation workers in Uttar Pradesh have become millionaires. They receive a monthly salary of ₹42,000 from the government. Some own marriage halls, while others own cement agencies and dozens of shops. One even owns a petrol pump. These workers do not sweep streets or clean drains. Instead, they have hired labourers on daily wages of ₹300 to ₹400 to clean villages on their behalf. An investigation by Dainik Bhaskar has exposed a syndicate involving these sanitation workers. Inputs were coming in from several districts, and Bhaskar selected Lakhimpur, the largest district in Uttar Pradesh, for its investigation. It emerged that the racket operates with the alleged connivance of village heads and secretaries. Five key findings from the sting operation: There are currently 94,000 sanitation workers employed in Uttar Pradesh. Those caught on camera during the Bhaskar investigation had joined the service in 2008 or later. After being made permanent during the Akhilesh government, some gradually set up businesses of their own. In collusion with village heads and officials, they get daily-wage labourers to clean villages for just two or three days. These workers are paid ₹300 to ₹400 a day. This allows a sanitation worker drawing a monthly salary of ₹42,000 to save ₹4.5 lakh a year. Several workers also give a share of this money to the village head, as the latter has the authority to approve the duty roster. At Bailha gram panchayat in Nighasan block of Lakhimpur, Dinesh Jaiswal owns a marriage hall spread across six bighas and a Jaiswal Automobile agency. As a sanitation worker, Dinesh is posted in Bailha village, 55 km away. We found Dinesh personally handling bookings at the marriage hall. A conversation with an employee, Sarthak, revealed that Dinesh had bought the land in 2020 at ₹19 lakh per bigha. He then built the marriage hall at a cost of ₹2 crore. Reporter: We want to book the marriage hall. How much will it cost? Please see if you can offer us a lower rate. Dinesh: Brother, it will cost ₹60,000. I am telling you right now. We have also come up from humble beginnings. Reporter: Your employees were telling us that you are a sanitation worker. Dinesh: Yes, I am. So what? I won't sit here myself. Brother will sit here. Our duty hours are from 8 am to 3 pm and from 7 am to 2 pm. After that, I can sit here at the marriage hall, can't I? Dinesh had hired Ashok Valmiki to sweep Bailha village. While looking for Ashok, we met Sandeep Valmiki, who had also worked as a sanitation worker for Dinesh earlier. To understand the entire arrangement, we approached Sandeep pretending to be a sanitation worker. Sandeep said Dinesh paid him ₹300 a day. According to Sandeep, he had to work only one or two days a week. The reporter told him that we were being transferred to Nighasan block and needed someone to clean a village. Sandeep then introduced us to Ashok Valmiki. Reporter: Where are you working at present? Ashok: I am working at a college now, but I had left the job earlier because the pay was too low. Reporter: Have you worked for any sanitation worker before? Ashok: Yes, I have worked for Jawwad, Heeralal and Dinesh Jaiswal. Dinesh was posted in Bailha. Reporter: How much was Dinesh paying you? Ashok: Look, when I travelled in my own vehicle, he paid me ₹450. When he took me along in his vehicle, he paid me ₹400. It is 20 km from Nighasan. I had to go there for 15 days a month. Sometimes he paid me monthly, while at other times he settled the amount on a daily basis. Reporter: Are you still working for him? Did he go to the village himself or not? Ashok: No, I worked for him until two or three months ago. Why would he go there himself? He has a separate arrangement. He is wealthy, and his brother is an excise inspector. Ashok said: "Only the main areas need to be cleaned, along with the village head's house." Reporter: So you don't have to go there every day? Ashok: We only have to clean the main areas, such as the village head's house. During festivals, we have to clean the entire house. Reporter: Does nobody come to check? Ashok: No, nobody checks. You can get the work done in Bailha village. There are one or two other villages, but don't go there. If a roster-based duty is assigned there, the village head gives the sanitation worker a hard time. For example, if four people are assigned to duty, you have to bring all four. Otherwise, the work will not be done. Reporter: How much will you charge us per day? Ashok: I will charge ₹400 a day. If you call me, I will come even in an emergency. I have an Apache motorcycle. I don't drink alcohol or take drugs. I only chew paan. I am currently working for five sanitation workers. Reporter: How much do you collect from them every month? Ashok: ₹12,000. Reporter: Then you must have become a millionaire by now. Ashok: I work hard. What millionaire? You people are sanitation workers now. When floods occur, we don't go there for six months. It is then that we have to finish all the work. We then approached another sanitation worker, Virendra Kumar. He is posted in Grant No. 12 village in Nighasan block. Virendra owns an ACC Cement agency as well as a shopping complex. He has rented out half a dozen shops, and one building has been leased to Indian Bank. A Bhaskar reporter met Virendra at one of the shops in the shopping complex, posing as a sanitation worker. Reporter: It would be good if I could get some work. You could put me in your place at Grant No. 12. Virendra: Yes, there is already someone there. Reporter: You could pay me a little less than what you pay the other person. Virendra: There is nothing like that. We just pay daily wages. The roster is in place, and the work continues on a permanent basis. Reporter: So, people from which village are working for you? Virendra: They are from that area itself, from Srinagar village. Reporter: How much do you pay the people you have hired for cleaning? Virendra: We pay them ₹300 or ₹350 a day. We need them when there is more work. Anil Valmiki had been cleaning Grant No. 12 village in Nighasan block for Virendra Kumar. He left the job three months ago. His father, Jhabbu Lal, had also worked as a labourer for Virendra. In the same village, we met Mangal Singh Yadav, who works as an Aapda Mitra (disaster response volunteer). According to Mangal, two local youths, Arjun and Anil, used to clean the village for Virendra. Arjun has since died, while Anil has gone to jail. Virendra used to pay him ₹300 a day. Now, Virendra brings labourers from Nighasan. Reporter: Virendra is quite a wealthy man. Mangal: Yes, he has shops on the embankment. There is a bank operating on the ground floor of his house. Reporter: Does he ever come to work himself? Mangal: He does come, but you know that there is always work at the school. The cleaning is not done every day. Workers posted in urban areas and along the main highway get the work done daily because some official or another keeps visiting those places. That is why they are cleaned every day. But here, they come only two or three times a week. Reporter: Do you know Rajesh, who sits at a computer in the ADO office? Mangal: Yes, I know him. His father used to sit with us. We have been watching the block since 2009. There is no official who does not know me. Reporter: Rajesh is also quite influential. His father has been the village head three times. He has also set up several firms. Mangal: Yes, they manufacture interlocking bricks. Reporter: The officials must know about all this. Since the village was washed away, there must be hardly any work left. Everything must be happening only on paper. Mangal: Yes, exactly. Grant was washed away last year. Now, only around 100 to 150 houses may be left. Reporter: But sanitation workers are still posted there. Mangal: Yes. Among the sanitation workers, Hargovind Yadav is the most influential. Reporter: What does he own? Mangal: He is into property plotting. He buys and sells land. His brother's name is Chandrapal, who used to live in Grant. Now, he has even set up a petrol pump and other businesses. Reporter: Could it be that his family supports him financially? Mangal: No, he started plotting only after joining the job. The petrol pump has been opened in his wife's name. After speaking to Mangal, we learnt about two more workers, Hargovind and Rajesh Kumar. Anil used to clean the village for Virendra, and Mangal gave us his mobile number. A Bhaskar reporter spoke to Anil to understand the entire arrangement involving Virendra. Reporter: Did you clean the village regularly or only occasionally? Were you paid monthly? Anil: They paid me for the days they called me. I had been working for him ever since he was posted there. He paid me ₹300. Reporter: How much would you earn in a month? You must have had to go there at least 10 to 12 days. Anil: There were several places where work had to be done every day. The village head would call me daily, but he would not pay me. Hargovind is a sanitation worker who is also involved in the property business. So, a Bhaskar reporter approached him on the pretext of buying a plot. He said he was posted as a sanitation worker in Adlabad, Lakhimpur, but owned a petrol pump worth ₹1.5 crore and was also involved in property dealing. He claimed to have sold plots to most of the block officials. Reporter: What do you do? Hargovind: I am a rural sanitation worker in this panchayat. We do property business in my wife's name. Why should I hide anything from you? Our petrol pump has been approved in Lakhimpur. I am also posted in Adlabad, where our bricks are being made. That is why I don't go there very often. Reporter: Do you also own a brick kiln? Hargovind: No, it is the village head's plant. We are getting bricks made there. We earn around ₹1.5 lakh. Reporter: Don't you face any problems with your duty? Hargovind: No, we don't do it in our own name. We do it in my wife's name and also file income tax returns. Our duty lasts until 2 pm. After that, we are free. Reporter: How will you manage the work once the petrol pump starts operating? Hargovind: Brother, it is very difficult. There was a small problem with the site plan. We have spent ₹8 lakh to ₹10 lakh, including some money through unofficial channels. We still had to get the NOC. We have submitted the papers to the fire department and the traffic department. Reporter: Where are you opening the petrol pump? There must have been a tender or something. Hargovind: We are opening it in Lakhimpur. It is a semi-government setup. Government employees cannot apply for it. This is our first time, so we have invested ₹1.5 crore to ₹2 crore. Reporter: Petrol pumps earn a commission per litre. Hargovind: My brother-in-law also owns a pump. It sells 8,000 litres a day. So, you can understand that we earn ₹20,000 a day. My brother-in-law is a doctor and a government employee. My wife has a BMS degree, so they have set up a hospital. It was established in 2023, and we have received our turn now. We had got approval for a pump in Belaparsua in 2017, but we did not set it up. Kisnu Valmiki is a resident of Adlabad village, where Hargovind is posted. Kisnu cleans the village on Hargovind's behalf. We spoke to him over the phone, posing as a sanitation worker. Reporter: Do you work for Hargovind as a sanitation worker? Kisnu: Yes, I have been working for him for two years. Reporter: How much do you get paid? Kisnu: He pays ₹500 for two or three hours of work. Reporter: Would there be any problem if we did not come ourselves? Kisnu: No, there would be no problem. We learnt that Rajesh is posted in Mahadev Mudiya, under Grant No. 12 gram panchayat, but the hamlet has been washed away due to river erosion. In this situation, Rajesh Kumar has been attached to the ADO office. His uncle, Suresh Kumar, told us that Rajesh had earlier served as the village head and was preparing to contest the election again. Rajesh owns a cement-brick factory. We wanted to meet him posing as a customer, but found him sitting at a computer desk in the block office. Reporter: How much would it cost if we set up this plant? Rajesh: It would cost around ₹20 lakh to start with. Reporter: You would be able to do business mainly with village heads, wouldn't you? Rajesh: Yes, it would mainly be with village heads. Reporter: What would be the price of cement bricks? Rajesh: If you collect them yourself, they will cost ₹11 each. I can reduce the price by 25 paise. If we deliver them, you will have to pay the transportation cost. It will be around ₹1.25 per brick. This conversation made it clear that Rajesh was connected to the cement-brick business.

stories.title: 58 out of 100 train ticket booking attempts are fake:Automated software is behind the scam; how seats get filled within 2 minutes
stories.summary: Passengers travelling home for Chhath are facing mounting difficulties. Railway stations are overcrowded, with trains from major cities such as Delhi and Mumbai to Lucknow, Gorakhpur and Varanasi packed to capacity. There is little to no room even to stand. Surprisingly, many passengers who tried to book tickets two months in advance were also unable to get confirmed seats. Those now relying on Tatkal tickets are facing similar problems. Seats are getting filled within one or two minutes of the booking window opening. In several cases, money is being deducted from passengers' accounts, but they are still not getting confirmed tickets. So, where do the tickets disappear as soon as the booking window opens? Does someone book them before passengers get a chance? Why does the railway repeatedly fail to make adequate arrangements during festivals? Let's find out in this UP Explainer. Question 1: Are illegal ticket agents booking all the tickets before passengers can? Answer: Data presented in Parliament in July 2026 shows that the IRCTC ticket-booking system is facing more attacks from bots (automated software) than bookings by genuine passengers. Illegal ticket agents use these systems to manipulate the booking process. According to the Ministry of Railways, the online ticket-booking system received 15.38 billion requests between January and June 2026. Of these, 8.88 billion, or 57.74%, were made through automated software. During June, the summer holiday period, this figure exceeded 66%. According to the Railways, its e-ticketing system prevented these requests from booking tickets. Automated software saves passengers' names, ages, train numbers and payment details even before bookings open. As soon as general or Tatkal quota bookings begin, the software continuously sends requests to the IRCTC system and books seats before ordinary passengers can fill in the forms. Earlier, software such as Nexus, Red Mirchi and Super Tatkal was widely used. These were completely shut down following action by the Railways and the Railway Protection Force (RPF) against illegal agents in 2020. However, similar software is still active under new names and with modified technology. An ordinary passenger takes around two minutes to log in to the IRCTC portal, enter details, fill in the CAPTCHA and make the payment. These software programmes complete the entire process in just a few seconds. They can also bypass CAPTCHA codes. The Railways and IRCTC use advanced cybersecurity systems to detect such software. A human being has a natural pattern of moving a mouse and typing on a keyboard, whereas a bot can fill in an entire form within a millisecond. If the typing speed is detected to be in milliseconds, the Railways blocks the booking request. If dozens of accounts on the same internet network attempt to book tickets simultaneously, the system detects the activity. Accounts that reach the payment stage within two to three seconds are also blocked. With stricter action against automated software and tighter rules for IRCTC accounts not verified through Aadhaar, illegal agents have found another way around the restrictions. Large-scale agents have collected genuine Aadhaar cards and mobile numbers from hundreds of ordinary people in villages and small towns and created accounts in their names. They now hire 20–30 young men to sit at computers and book tickets manually at high speed instead of using software. To the system, these appear to be genuine passengers. However, there are several other reasons why passengers fail to get tickets. Question 2: What are the other reasons passengers fail to get confirmed tickets? Answer: The main reasons are the Railways' quota system and the large number of people trying to book tickets online simultaneously. A typical express train has around 22 to 24 coaches, with a total of 1,400 to 1,700 seats. Of these, three to four are general coaches (unreserved). Only the remaining coaches have reserved seats. However, not all these seats are made available to ordinary passengers when advance bookings open. For advance bookings, which open 60 days before the journey, only a portion of the total seats is made available to the general public under the general quota at 8 am. The remaining seats are reserved for Tatkal, women, senior citizens and passengers boarding at other major stations along the route. The Railways wants to ensure that people travelling from all small and large towns along a train's route, as well as those travelling at short notice, women, senior citizens and sick passengers, can also get seats. Therefore, it divides the total number of seats into different categories or quotas. The general quota is the largest in express trains. Around 50% to 60% of the total seats under this quota are allocated to passengers travelling from the starting station to the final destination. For example, if a train runs from Delhi to Gorakhpur via Lucknow, the Railways will reserve more seats for passengers travelling from Delhi to Gorakhpur than for those travelling only from Delhi to Lucknow. This is because if the Railways allocates more seats to passengers travelling from Delhi to Lucknow, those seats may remain vacant beyond Lucknow until Gorakhpur, resulting in a loss for the Railways. In addition, 10% to 30% of the seats in each class are reserved under the Tatkal quota for passengers who need to travel at short notice. Some lower berths are reserved for women travelling alone, pregnant women and senior citizens. Apart from this, around 2% to 5% of seats are kept under the emergency or VIP quota for ministers, MPs, government officials, railway employees and passengers facing medical emergencies. On top of this, millions of people across the country try to book tickets at 8 am during the festival season. One user can book up to six tickets at a time. As a result, the limited number of general quota seats gets filled within just two to three minutes. The situation is similar with the Tatkal quota. Thousands and lakhs of genuine passengers across the country compete simultaneously for just 100–150 seats. When one lakh genuine passengers are competing for 150 seats, tickets will sell out within seconds even without any automated software. Question 3: How can passengers travel in reserved coaches if they do not have confirmed tickets? Answer: If you have purchased a waiting-list ticket from a railway reservation counter, you can travel only in a general (unreserved) coach with that ticket. You cannot travel in a sleeper or AC coach. If you board a reserved coach and the TTE finds a vacant seat, they may allow you to occupy it after collecting the applicable penalty or fare difference. Otherwise, you will be asked to move to the general coach. If you have booked an online ticket and it does not get confirmed or reach RAC status by the time the chart is prepared, the e-ticket will be automatically cancelled and the money will be refunded to your account. If you board even the general coach with such a ticket, you will be treated as a passenger travelling without a ticket. The TTE may impose a penalty and ask you to get off at the next station. Under the Railways' new rules, the first reservation chart is prepared eight hours before the train's departure, while the final chart is prepared around 30 minutes before departure. Any seats left vacant under the VIP and other quotas are then used to confirm waiting-list tickets. If seats are still vacant after this, they are sold under 'Current Availability'. Passengers can book these seats through the IRCTC app, website or the station's current reservation counter, from four hours to 30 minutes before the train departs. Passengers should also select the VIKALP option while booking tickets. If their ticket remains on the waiting list, the Railways may allot them a confirmed seat on another train on the same route, subject to availability. Passengers can also check seat availability on other trains running along the same route themselves. As mentioned earlier, the Railways allocates separate quotas for different stations. If a ticket from your city shows a waiting list, try checking availability from a major station located 50–100 km before your city. If a confirmed seat is available from there, you can book the ticket from that station and select the 'Change Boarding Point' option to board the train from your own station. The Railways also operates hundreds of festival special trains to manage the rush during festivals and holidays. Passengers are often unaware of these services. Such trains can be checked on the official NTES app, which has a separate section for them. When searching for trains on the IRCTC app or website after entering the date of travel, trains whose numbers begin with zero (such as 04012) are special trains. Passengers can also get updates about newly announced special trains through the X accounts of the Ministry of Railways and regional railway zones, such as Northern Railway and North Eastern Railway. Question 4: What changes has the Railways made to prevent ticket-booking fraud? Why does the problem persist? Answer: The Railways has taken several steps over the past one to two years to prevent ticket-booking fraud. CRIS (Centre for Railway Information Systems), the IT wing of the Railways, has continuously increased server capacity and bandwidth. The system is now claimed to be capable of booking more than 30,000 tickets per minute. It has also set a record of booking more than 1.6 million tickets in a single day. However, the growth in traffic is faster than the rate at which server capacity is being increased. Between January 2024 and June 2026, more than 66.8 million user IDs linked to suspicious mobile numbers, email addresses and IP addresses were deactivated. More than 13,000 email addresses used to create fake IDs were also blocked. Advanced network firewalls and AI-powered anti-bot tools have been installed outside the system to block suspicious traffic. To improve passenger convenience and transparency, the Railways has launched a new super app called RailOne. It is also upgrading its entire Passenger Reservation System (PRS) with advanced technology to speed up bookings and provide more accurate waiting-list predictions. The aim is also to offer reserved and unreserved ticket bookings, along with complaint-related services, through a single app. Despite these improvements, the experience of ordinary passengers remains caught between the Railways' claims and the ground reality. This means the problem has two aspects: A) Although the Railways' anti-bot technology prevents 58% of bots from booking tickets, millions of bots attempting to book tickets within the same second can still overload the servers. As a result, genuine passengers are left staring at a loading screen. B) According to the Ministry of Railways, 89% of tickets are booked online. The number of genuine passengers competing for a limited number of seats is so high that even if bots are completely eliminated, the scramble for tickets during festivals and on busy routes will continue.

stories.title: 'Win even one seat and I'll do whatever you ask':Chandrashekhar's ex-girlfriend Rohini challenges new alliance
stories.summary: Chandrashekhar's ex-girlfriend Rohini Ghavari has launched a sharp attack after his alliance with Owaisi's party in Uttar Pradesh. In a three-minute video, Rohini said, "Let Chandrashekhar and Owaisi's Samajik Parivartan Morcha show that they can win even one seat in Uttar Pradesh. Then, I will be ready to do whatever he says." In fact, today, Thursday, Asaduddin Owaisi's AIMIM and Chandrashekhar's Azad Samaj Party (Kanshi Ram) jointly formed the Samajik Parivartan Morcha. The alliance has announced that it will field candidates in all 403 seats in the 2027 Assembly elections. Read what else Rohini Ghavri said The outcome of this alliance will also be zero An alliance was formed in Delhi and Bihar as well. Now, an alliance has also been formed in Uttar Pradesh. The similarity among all three is that the electoral result was zero. The result of this alliance in Uttar Pradesh will also be zero. Until yesterday, Owaisi was questioning Akhilesh Yadav while presenting himself as a well-wisher of Muslims, asking, "When will Abdul become chief minister? How long will he continue spreading carpets?" But now he himself has declared Chandrashekhar as the chief ministerial face of the alliance. Why Did Owaisi Not Announce a Muslim Chief Minister? Rohini questioned Owaisi's claim of being a well-wisher of Muslims. She asked why he had not announced that, if the government was formed, a Dalit would serve as chief minister for two and a half years and a Muslim for the next two and a half years. She said it was wrong to describe Chandrashekhar as a leader of Dalits. She also accused him of conspiring against BSP chief Mayawati and distributing books opposing her. According to Rohini, an attempt is being made through this alliance to mislead Dalits and Muslims. Chandrashekhar-Owaisi alliance is the BJP's B-team Rohini took a jibe at Chandrashekhar being named the chief ministerial face. She said, "Today, the happiness of becoming chief minister was clearly visible on his face." Describing the alliance as the BJP's B-team, she said that the people of UP and the Muslim community know whom they need to stand with.

stories.title: Azam Khan taken into 4-day ED custody:To be brought to Lucknow from Dasna jail for questioning over Jauhar University funds and land transactions
stories.summary: The CBI court in Ghaziabad has ordered that Mohammad Azam Khan, the Samajwadi Party heavyweight and former cabinet minister lodged in Dasna Jail, be handed over to the Enforcement Directorate (ED) on four-day remand. The ED had applied to the court on Thursday for seven days' remand. The court granted four days' remand. Following the remand order, Azam Khan will now be brought to the ED office in Lucknow, where he will be questioned. During these four days, the ED will question him about the amount spent on the construction of the university, the financial transactions of the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust and the purchase and sale of land. The case is not limited to alleged land grabbing; it also concerns the alleged use of government resources and contractors' money in the construction of the university. The ED's investigation has also uncovered alleged undeclared construction expenditure of around ₹416 crore. What is the full case? The ED's investigation began with 26 FIRs registered at the Ajimnagar police station in Rampur in July 2019. The cases alleged that the agricultural land of farmers in Singhan Kheda village was forcibly seized for the construction of Jauhar University. The farmers were allegedly threatened and pressured into registering the land in the university's name. Based on these cases, the ED began a money-laundering investigation. Allegation that no account was found for ₹416 crore in expenditure The ED's investigation revealed a major discrepancy in the expenditure incurred on the construction of Jauhar University. The Income Tax Department's valuation report assessed the value of the university's buildings at around ₹494.46 crore. The trust's income-tax returns showed capital expenditure of only ₹78.32 crore between 2013-14 and 2024-25. The difference between the two figures is around ₹416.14 crore. The ED suspects that the source of the funds used in the university's construction is unclear. The agency is investigating the discrepancy. Role of government funds and contractors also under investigation The Enforcement Directorate (ED) alleges that funds and materials allocated for government construction projects were used at Jauhar University while Azam Khan was a Cabinet minister. According to the investigating agency, some contractors who secured government contracts used construction materials and funds for building the university. The agency is also investigating donations made by some contractors to the Jauhar Trust. The ED has further claimed that hostels, a hospital and other construction projects were carried out on the university campus through the Jal Nigam. It has emerged that government funds were spent on these construction projects. Property worth ₹426 crore already attached In this case, the ED took steps to attach Jauhar University's land and buildings on 28 October. At the time, the university's estimated market value was assessed at ₹1,170 crore and its government value at ₹426.46 crore, following which the university was attached. These properties are in the name of the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust. Azam Khan established the trust and is its founder and controller. Questions the ED will seek answers to Where did the money allegedly accounting for the discrepancy of more than ₹416 crore in the construction of Jauhar University come from? On whose instructions were government funds and materials used in the construction of the university? What financial transactions took place between the contractors who secured government contracts and the Jauhar Trust? What was the actual source of the donations received by the trust, and where were they used? Which people played a role in purchasing farmers' land for the university and allegedly taking possession of enemy property? Azam was arrested again minutes after his release Azam Khan was released from Rampur jail on 31 October after being granted bail in two PAN card cases. However, as soon as he walked out of the jail, the Enforcement Directorate arrested him in a money-laundering case linked to Jauhar University. On 1 November, a special PMLA court in Ghaziabad sent him to Dasna jail in 14-day judicial custody. The ED subsequently sought seven days' custody remand for questioning. The court has now approved four days of remand.

stories.title: 3 children from one family die within 3 days:2 collapsed while playing, third developed fever; blood came from all three children's mouths
stories.summary: Three children from the same family died within three days in Lucknow. The first two died after falling while playing. The third child died some time after developing a fever. According to the family, blood was coming from all three children's mouths before they died. The first two children were not subjected to post-mortem examinations. After the third child's death, the police sent the body for a post-mortem examination. Villagers have demanded a thorough investigation into the matter by the Health Department and the administration. The incident took place in Khandsara village in the Malihabad area. See 3 pictures... Read the full story... Two children cremated without post-mortems Ashish, a resident of Khandsara village, is a farmer. He lives with his maternal grandfather Kishan Kumar, mother Nirmala, wife Anjali and three children: Lakshmi (10), Kartik (7) and Devansh (3). All three of his children died suddenly, one after another, over the past three days. According to the information available, his youngest son Divyansh suddenly collapsed while playing on 9 November. The family took him to hospital, where he died. They cremated him without having any tests conducted. Daughter's health suddenly deteriorated The following morning, on 10 November, his second son Kartik also suddenly collapsed while playing. The family took him to hospital, but he could not be saved. The family cremated him as well. He was a Year 1 student. Meanwhile, on 12 November, Ashish's elder daughter, Lakshmi, suddenly fell ill. She developed a fever in the morning. Her family took her to Seva Hospital, where she died during treatment. Daughter's body sent for post-mortem After Lakshmi's death, her family informed the police and requested a post-mortem examination. Police reached the spot after receiving the information, took the body into custody and sent it for a post-mortem examination. The cause of death will become clear only after the post-mortem report is released. Developed a mild fever, then died Ashish's maternal grandfather, Kishan Kumar, said he had developed a mild fever in the morning, but it subsided afterwards. They had just brought him to the hospital when he died. Devansh was the first to die. Kartik died afterwards, and today, Thursday, Lakshmi also died. Meanwhile, Mal Community Health Centre superintendent Dhanjay Kushwaha said a team had been sent to the centre. He said nothing could be confirmed until its report was received. Villagers suspect witchcraft The family members said blood came from the mouths of all three children when they died. After the first two children suddenly collapsed while playing and died in similar circumstances, various discussions began among the villagers. Following the third death, some villagers are now also suspecting witchcraft. The village is in mourning following the deaths of three children from the same family. The villagers have demanded that the Health Department and the administration conduct a serious investigation into the matter. The actual cause of the deaths will emerge only after the post-mortem reports.

stories.title: Accused's house being demolished after Lucknow triple murder:3 people were shot dead in broad daylight; family had sought bulldozer action
stories.summary: A bulldozer is once again being used at the house of Rishabh Shukla, the accused in the broad daylight triple murder in Lucknow's Saadatganj. The LDA team has arrived to carry out the action with a heavy police presence. A bulldozer had been used at the accused's house earlier as well. At that time, only the boundary wall was demolished. The victim's family and local residents had expressed their displeasure over this. After the incident, Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak had also visited the victim's family. He had assured them that action would be taken. On the morning of 26 October, a dispute broke out in Saadatganj between Rishabh Shukla's family and Shivaji Tiwari's family over the construction of a raised platform. Rishabh allegedly shot dead Shivaji, his son and his brother. The police arrested him at the spot. See three pictures... Triple murder was committed over a car parking and platform dispute A dispute had arisen in Brahman Tola in Saadatganj over car parking and a platform. In this dispute, Rishabh Shukla (30) shot dead three people. Among the deceased was Shivaji Tiwari (62), a retired Secretariat employee. He had also served as the RSS district co-organiser. His brother, Shivendra Tiwari, alias Shambhu, worked at Lucknow University. Son's wedding was scheduled for 5 December Shivaji Tiwari's son, Suyash (30), was in the electrical goods business. His wedding was scheduled for 5 December. The killings turned the family's celebrations into mourning. DGP had assured the victim's family On the fifth day after the incident, DGP Rajeev Krishna met the victim's family. Usha Tiwari, the wife of the deceased Shivaji, demanded that the accused be sentenced to death. The victim's family demanded that bulldozers be used to demolish the accused's house. The LDA demolished part of the boundary wall with a bulldozer after finding that it extended into the road. During this, the family alleged that not only the accused's boundary wall but also the house had been built on Nazul land.

stories.title: Hoardings put up in Lucknow ahead of Akhilesh's Ayodhya visit:New meaning of PDA explained; resolve to make him CM in 2027
stories.summary: A new hoarding put up outside the Samajwadi Party office in Lucknow on Thursday has drawn attention. It gives a new meaning to PDA for SP president Akhilesh Yadav. The hoarding says P stands for "Pehle", D for "Darshan" and A for "Aashirwad". It was put up ahead of Akhilesh Yadav's proposed visit to Ayodhya on 12 December. The hoarding refers to a visit to Ayodhya while addressing Akhilesh Yadav as "Adarniya". It has been put up in the name of Abdul Azim Mansoori. Through it, a message has been conveyed linking Akhilesh's visit to Ayodhya with respect and blessings. PDA described as a message of taking everyone along Samajwadi Party leader Mohammad Azim, who had the hoardings installed, said Akhilesh Yadav was a leader who took everyone along. He respected the elderly and, along with young people, was also concerned about the future of the coming generation. According to him, PDA itself means taking every section of society along. With this outlook, efforts are being made to bring all communities together under the SP flag. Resolve to make Akhilesh chief minister in 2027 Mohammad Azim said the people associated with PDA had resolved to make Akhilesh Yadav chief minister in 2027. PDA is not merely a political slogan but a mission to secure justice for Dalits, backward classes and the oppressed. He claimed that, riding on the PDA chariot, Akhilesh Yadav would write a new chapter in the state's development.

stories.title: Mobile worth ₹20,000 stolen in 15 seconds in Varanasi:Thief slips it into bag from shop counter; CCTV captures incident
stories.summary: Two clever thieves posing as customers targeted a mobile phone shop in Kachhwa Road market, in Varanasi's Mirzamurad police station area, on Wednesday night and fled with an expensive smartphone. The entire theft was captured on the shop's CCTV camera. The two men arrived at the shop together at around 6.45 p.m. and asked the shopkeeper to show them mobile phones. As the shopkeeper began showing them the phones, the man wearing a red hoodie put one of them in his bag within 15 seconds. The phone was valued at ₹20,000. The police are currently investigating the incident and searching for the thieves using the CCTV footage. Distracted the shopkeeper with conversation before carrying out the theft The owner of New Mahesh Mobile Shop on Kachhwa Road, Mahesh Gupta, said two youths posing as customers came to his shop at around 7 p.m. on Wednesday night. On the pretext of buying a mobile phone, they asked him to show them several new phones kept on the counter. While the shopkeeper was busy showing them the phones, one of the youths kept him engaged in conversation. Meanwhile, taking advantage of the opportunity, the other youth carefully picked up a new Ai+ Nova 2 Pro 5G smartphone from the counter and put it in his bag. The two youths then fled the spot within moments. Thieves' actions captured on CCTV Mahesh said that shortly after the thieves left, he noticed that phones were missing when he began checking the stock. He immediately examined the footage from the CCTV cameras installed in the shop. The footage clearly shows one young man picking up a mobile phone from the counter and putting it in his shoulder bag, while his accomplice tries to distract the shopkeeper. Police begin investigation into the case As soon as he learnt about the incident, victimised shopkeeper Mahesh Gupta reached the police booth on Kachhwa Road. There, he provided Mirzamurad Station House Officer Gopal Ji Kushwaha and Outpost In-Charge Sandeep Kumar Singh with written and oral details of the entire incident and had his statement recorded. The Station House Officer took prompt action and asked the shopkeeper to send the CCTV footage to the Outpost In-Charge's WhatsApp number. Upon receiving the information, a police team reached the spot, inspected the scene and began an investigation. Police said they were trying to identify the two unidentified thieves on the basis of the CCTV footage.

stories.title: Applications open for teacher awards in Gorakhpur:Teachers of govt and aided schools can apply till November 30
stories.summary: The application process for the State Teacher Award and Chief Minister's Teacher Award has begun for teachers who have performed outstanding teaching work in Gorakhpur. Eligible teachers and principals in the district can apply online until 30 November. The Secondary Education Department has released the complete schedule, from applications to final selection, for the 2026-27 academic session. The application process will be conducted online. Interested teachers can visit the Madhyamik Shiksha Parishad website, upmsp.edu.in, and fill in their forms. The department has clarified that offline applications will not be accepted. Teachers at government and aided schools will get an opportunity Principals, headmasters, lecturers and assistant teachers of government and non-government aided secondary schools will be eligible to apply for the State Teacher Award. Teachers from aided Sanskrit schools are also included in this category. Meanwhile, principals, headmasters and teachers of non-government unaided, or private, secondary schools will be eligible to apply for the Chief Minister's Teacher Award. Document verification will begin in December The next stage of the selection process will begin after the application process is completed on 30 November. From 1 to 15 December, the district-level committee will scrutinise the teachers' applications and documents. Their claims and achievements will also undergo physical verification during this period. Thereafter, from 16 to 30 December, the divisional-level committee will send its selection proposals to the directorate after completing the scrutiny. Final selection in January In the final stage of the selection process, all proposals will be sent from the directorate level to the state-level committee between 31 December and 14 January 2027. The state-level committee will then review the applications and make the final selection from 15 to 24 January. Thus, the entire process, from application to final selection, will be completed in January. The department has appealed to all eligible teachers to apply online within the stipulated time.

stories.title: UP declares holiday for Guru Tegh Bahadur martyrdom day:Offices to remain closed on December 14; Saturday closure would mean a 3-day break
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government has changed the date of the public holiday marking Guru Tegh Bahadur's martyrdom day. The holiday will now be observed on December 14 instead of November 24. Government offices will remain closed for three days, as November 12 is the second Saturday and December 13 is a Sunday. However, offices that do not observe a holiday on the second Saturday will remain closed for two days. Last year, on November 17, 2025, the government released its list of public holidays for 2026. It had initially declared November 24 as a holiday to mark Guru Tegh Bahadur's martyrdom day. Holiday shifted to Monday, rest of calendar unchanged In its revised order, the government has changed only the date of the holiday marking Guru Tegh Bahadur's martyrdom day. November 24 also marks Guru Nanak Jayanti and Kartik Purnima. According to the government calendar, it will remain a public holiday. The government has clarified that only this date has been revised in the annual holiday list. All other holidays in the calendar will remain unchanged. Reason behind change in date The government notification does not mention the reason for changing the date. However, the main reason is believed to be the calculations based on the traditional calendar (Nanakshahi calendar). According to Sikh traditions and the original Nanakshahi calendar, Guru Tegh Bahadur's martyrdom day is observed on Shukla Panchami, which falls on December 14 in 2026. Earlier, the date was listed as November 24 based on the Gregorian calendar. In view of demands from the Sikh community, the government has revised the holiday from November 24 to December 14 (Monday).

stories.title: Shivpal meets Azam Khan in jail after Akhilesh:Says he will share details after meeting; over 400 SP workers gather outside
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party national general secretary Shivpal Yadav reached Ghaziabad on Wednesday. He arrived at Dasna Jail around 10:30 am to meet party leader Azam Khan, who is lodged there. More than 400 Samajwadi Party workers gathered outside the jail. Party leaders welcomed Shivpal and raised slogans of "Shivpal Yadav zindabad" and "Azam Khan zindabad". Shivpal asked the workers to remain calm and spoke to the media. He said, "I will meet him now and ask about his well-being. After that, I will come out and speak to the media." After speaking to reporters, Shivpal went inside the jail. Shivpal completed formalities before meeting Azam Shivpal first met jail officials and completed the required formalities. He was then allowed to meet Azam Khan. The two leaders are currently talking inside the jail. According to sources, they may also discuss the Assembly elections. ED arrested Azam Khan in money-laundering case The Enforcement Directorate (ED) arrested Azam Khan on October 31 in a money-laundering case. He was arrested at the gate after coming out of Rampur Jail. On November 1, a special PMLA court sent him to 14 days of judicial custody. He has been lodged in Dasna Jail for the past 12 days. Earlier, SP national president Akhilesh Yadav met Azam Khan in jail on October 22. His wife, Tazeen Fatima, also met him on November 6. Wife Tanjeen Fatima reached Dasna Jail to meet him on 6 November On 6 November, Tanjeen Fatima reached Dasna Jail with her elder son, Adeeb Azam, and her adopted daughter, Ekta Kaushik. She met her husband, Azam Khan. After this, Tanjeen said, "Azam Khan, who has served as an MLA 10 times and as a Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha MP, is being kept amid filth in jail. He is being kept as if he might escape. A killer roams freely, but this is how Azam sahib is being treated." She said, "The court has been informed that Azam is not keeping well. He has suffered a stroke. All his medical reports have also been submitted to the court, yet he is being kept in such conditions in jail." What case has the ED arrested Azam in? Read what happened after Azam was released from jail On 29 October, the High Court suspended the 10-year sentences handed to Azam and his son Abdullah in the two PAN card cases and granted bail to both of them. They were released from Rampur jail at around 7:15 p.m. on the evening of 31 October, after 11 months. Fifteen minutes before he came out, a team from the ED entered the jail. A heated argument broke out at the jail's main gate between the officers, who arrived in a white car, and Azam's lawyers. During this, Azam also answered the officers' questions, but the matter was not resolved. The officers then took him away in their car. During this, Azam raised his hand towards the sky and said, "Allah is watching everything. What is there to say now? This is the punishment for being Muslim. The mistake is that a Muslim built a university. This is our sin." Outside Ghaziabad court, Azam had said: "What is left to say?" On 1 November, ED officers produced Azam before the special PMLA court in Ghaziabad. A total of 100 CRPF and police personnel were also deployed during the proceedings. Azam appeared quite calm when he arrived at the court premises. He only kept looking towards the people. As soon as he rolled down the car window, the media asked, "Won't you say anything?" He replied, "What is left to say?" The Supreme Court had refused to hear the bail plea The Supreme Court refused to hear Azam Khan's bail plea on 5 November. It also transferred his petition to the Allahabad High Court. The court told the Chief Justice of the High Court to list the case for hearing before a division bench before 16 November. The bench must pass an interim order on Azam's petition on 16 November itself. Azam had said: "They want to keep me in jail during the election" Azam told the court, "I will face every case, but I need bail. I am 80 years old. I was arrested in 28 other cases besides the ED case. At this rate, I will die in jail. They want to keep me in jail until the election." Azam did not appear before the Supreme Court himself. He made these submissions through his lawyer, Kapil Sibal.

stories.title: "I don't look beautiful, I should die":Gorakhpur Class 12 pass-out attempts suicide 3 times, parents worried
stories.summary: “I am 19 years old. Everyone says I am beautiful, but I find my face ugly when I look in the mirror. I have attempted suicide three times. Each time, I survived by luck.” A 19-year-old NEET aspirant from Basti told a psychologist in Gorakhpur this during a counselling session. Her parents remain deeply distressed by her repeated suicide attempts and are unable to sleep peacefully at night. One family member or another stays with her at all times. Family turns to psychologist after several treatments fail Her family had taken her to several doctors, but her condition did not improve. They eventually approached a psychologist. During counselling, it emerged that the student was suffering from body dysmorphic disorder. NEET preparation after scoring well in Class 12 Nitika (name changed), a resident of Basti, studied at a school in Gorakhpur until Class 12. After securing good marks in the Intermediate examination, she began preparing for NEET. Her mother is a teacher, while her father works as an administrative officer in a district of the state. ‘I have been struggling with my reflection for two years’ The student told the psychologist, "People wonder what is wrong with me. I do well in my studies, have friends at college and receive a lot of love from my family. But the truth is that I have been struggling with my reflection in the mirror every day for the past two years. "As soon as I wake up, the first thing I do is look in the mirror. I feel that my nose is crooked, my face looks terrible and my stomach sticks out. I also feel that my hair looks bad. I can spend an hour standing in front of the mirror, constantly trying to fix my appearance." She avoids showing her face in group photographs She said, "Sometimes I apply make-up, sometimes I use filters and at other times I keep adjusting my hair. When I go to college, I feel that everyone is looking at me and laughing at the flaws in my face. I sit at the back of the classroom so that no one can see me. "I am afraid of having my photograph taken. I even hide my face in group photographs. All this has made me feel that I no longer want to live." ‘She has even cut a vein in her hand’ Dr Aakriti Pandey said the student had been troubling her family for the past two years. She had attempted suicide three times. On one occasion, she had even cut a vein in her hand. She was treated at several places in Kanpur and Gorakhpur, but there was no significant improvement. In April 2026, her parents brought her to me. Counselling revealed that she was suffering from body dysmorphic disorder. She needed regular counselling. With the help of cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT), her condition improved significantly over seven months. Now, learn about two more such cases... 1. Attempted suicide because of facial pimples Rahul (name changed), an 18-year-old living in Gorakhpur's Gulriha area, has topped his school in Class 12. His father works in government service, while his mother is a housewife. Rahul has severe pimples on his face. Because of this, he hides his face from people. He once tried to commit suicide by jumping from the roof. His parents then consulted doctors and took him to a psychologist. Tests and counselling revealed that he was suffering from body dysmorphic disorder. He underwent treatment for around 12 months. His behaviour has improved considerably with psychotherapy. He is currently undergoing Ayurvedic treatment for the pimples. 2. "I look like a girl; I should die" Rohit, 19, who lives in Gorakhpur city, has attempted suicide twice. He feels that his body looks like a girl's. His father is a railway employee, while his mother is a homemaker. Rohit has suffered from obesity since childhood. He has a considerable amount of fat around his stomach and chest. Other students at school used to tease him because of this. At home, too, he spends the entire day looking at himself in the mirror. He also goes to the gym. He was recently admitted to a BTech course at a college in Kanpur. He attempted suicide there as well. Since then, his parents have been keeping him with them. He has been receiving psychotherapy for the past year, which has improved his behaviour. Now learn about the main symptoms of body dysmorphic disorder... What could be the causes? stories.title: Mother kills son, dies by suicide:Six-month-old girl was strangled in Siddharthnagar left after being believed dead
stories.summary: A woman allegedly strangled her one-and-a-half-year-old son to death in Siddharthnagar, Uttar Pradesh, before attempting to kill her six-month-old daughter in the same way. When the baby lost consciousness, the woman reportedly assumed she was dead and left her behind. She then died by suicide by hanging herself. The boy died, while the baby girl was found unconscious and was subsequently attended to. The woman was identified as Kajal (25), a native of Mehra village in Madhya Pradesh's Bhind district. She lived with her husband, Ramnaresh (27), their son Tiger and six-month-old daughter Khushi in a rented house in Ward No. 11 of Raghunath Nagar, under the Shohratgarh police station area in Siddharthnagar. Ramnaresh, originally from Talgaon village in Madhya Pradesh's Datia district, has been living in Siddharthnagar for the past five years. He supports the family by selling phulki, a local snack. Mother allegedly strangled son before attacking daughter According to the police, Kajal first strangled her one-and-a-half-year-old son, Tiger. She then allegedly strangled her six-month-old daughter, Khushi. The baby lost consciousness, following which Kajal reportedly assumed she had died. The woman then hanged herself. Police begin investigation into deaths After receiving information about the incident, police reached the spot and took the bodies of the woman and her son into custody for further proceedings. The six-month-old girl was found unconscious. Police are also gathering information about her condition. The reason behind the incident remains unclear. Police are questioning family members and local residents as part of the investigation. Post-mortem report to establish cause of deaths Circle Officer Mayank Dwivedi said police were investigating both deaths. The exact circumstances would become clear after the post-mortem reports are received. Police are examining all possible aspects to establish the reason behind the incident.

stories.title: Bride weeps all night as groom skips wedding:Groom refuses to marry over ₹2 lakh dowry; she keeps gazing at her Henna
stories.summary: A bride in Sambhal spent the night crying in her wedding attire after the groom refused to arrive with his wedding procession over a dowry demand on Wednesday. She kept looking at the mehendi on her hands and feet as she waited for the wedding that never took place. The bride's family had agreed to give the groom ₹5 lakh as dowry but had paid only ₹3 lakh. Four hours before the wedding, the groom called and refused to bring the wedding procession, demanding the remaining ₹2 lakh. He also returned the ₹3 lakh already received. The bride's family tried to persuade the groom's relatives over the phone for six hours, but their efforts failed. They subsequently filed a police complaint against the groom and his father. The incident took place in a village under the jurisdiction of a police station around 11 km from the district headquarters. See 2 pictures- Groom works in the scrap business; bride's father died three years ago The bride, Shania, is from Mohammadpur Tanda village. Her father, Babu Rihan, died three years ago. The groom, Aqib, is from Fitkari village in Meerut and works in the scrap business in Delhi. Shania's brother, Shuaib, also works as a labourer at a scrap warehouse in Delhi. The two families had met at a funeral in Mohammadpur Tanda village some time ago. During the meeting, the groom's family noticed Shania, and discussions about the marriage began. Food arranged for 1,000 guests; 400-500 had already eaten Shan Mohammad, the bride's uncle, said the wedding was scheduled for the night of November 11. The family had made arrangements for food for around 1,000 guests. Around 400-500 guests had already eaten, but the wedding procession never arrived. Groom's father demanded ₹2 lakh over the phone The bride's uncle said the groom's father, Salim, called at around 4 pm and informed the family that the wedding procession would not arrive. The family continued requesting him to reconsider until 10 pm, but he remained firm on his decision. He insisted that the procession would arrive only if the remaining ₹2 lakh in dowry was paid. The bride's family said it could not afford the additional amount and refused to pay. As a result, the wedding was called off and the food prepared for the guests went to waste. Bride says groom had refused three days before wedding too Shania Malik, also known as Sannu, said she had been in regular contact with the groom, who had initially agreed to marry her. She alleged that he had also refused to bring the wedding procession three days before the nikah. However, discussions between the two families followed, and the matter was resolved, with the groom agreeing to proceed with the marriage. On the day of the nikah, however, he again demanded the remaining ₹2 lakh and refused to arrive with the wedding procession.

stories.title: Premanand Maharaj rides Bullet:Visits Yamuna bank for spiritual practice; meets devotees after 34 days
stories.summary: Vrindavan religious leader Premanand Maharaj was seen riding a Bullet motorcycle on Wednesday, on the occasion of Bhai Dooj. He travelled to the banks of the Yamuna, where he meditated at a secluded spot. The location was inaccessible by car. As soon as devotees spotted the saint, they ran towards him, chanting 'Radhe-Radhe' and greeting him with folded hands. Premanand Maharaj raised both hands to bless them. After completing his meditation, he returned to the Yamuna Bihar Kunj Ashram. Devotees got to see him after 34 days. The Bullet motorcycle was being ridden by his disciple and former wrestler Rinku Singh. Other disciples accompanied them. See 3 pictures- Premanand Maharaj has been living in seclusion for months Saint Premanand Maharaj has been living in seclusion for the past few months. He is currently staying at the Yamuna Bihar Kunj Ashram, located near Belvan, across the Yamuna in Vrindavan. The ashram is spread over approximately 9.5 bighas. Most of the premises are covered with greenery, while construction occupies around 25% of the area. Premanand Maharaj also undergoes dialysis at the ashram. He was last seen on October 8 Premanand Maharaj was last seen on October 8, when he visited the Keli Kunj Ashram at 5 am. He stayed there for around 10 minutes before walking to meet his guru, Shri Hit Govind Sharan Maharaj, whose residence is around 150 metres away. After meeting his guru, he returned to his new Yamuna Bihar Kunj Ashram. Disciple died by jumping from the Keli Kunj Trust building On September 25, Premanand Maharaj's disciple Rasik Dulari Sharan died by jumping from the fourth floor of the Keli Kunj Trust building. His last rites were performed on the banks of the Yamuna on September 26. During the incident, his mother alleged that her son was not allowed to meet her. Rasik Dulari Sharan was originally from Jabalpur in Madhya Pradesh. He moved to Vrindavan two years ago and took initiation from Premanand Maharaj. Following this, he changed his name from Deepak Lodhi to Rasik Dulari Sharan.

stories.title: Kashi's air turns toxic as AQI reaches 315:Construction dust adds to pollution, DM warns agencies of action
stories.summary: Although the weather in Varanasi remains dry, the city's air is steadily deteriorating. Kashi's Air Quality Index (AQI) was recorded at 315 on Thursday morning, placing it in the very poor category. Rising pollution poses a risk to people's health. People, particularly those suffering from asthma and respiratory illnesses, need to remain alert. The city's temperature was recorded at 22 degrees Celsius on Thursday morning. Wind speed was 5 kilometres per hour and humidity stood at 70 per cent. According to BHU meteorologist Prof. Manoj Srivastava, the weather is likely to remain dry for the next one week. Therefore, there is currently little hope that rain will reduce pollution. Dust from construction work is also increasing pollution, along with firecrackers Firecrackers are not the only reason for the rise in air pollution in the city. Ongoing construction work and unplanned excavation at various locations are also polluting the air. Dust blowing from construction sites is adding to people's problems. District Magistrate Satyendra Kumar has fixed the accountability of the executing organisations and construction agencies in this regard. He has strictly instructed all agencies to comply with pollution-control standards during construction work. Fine to be imposed for negligence, DM warns The DM has made it clear that adequate arrangements must be made to control dust at all construction sites. Compliance with the prescribed standards will be mandatory during construction work. If negligence by any agency comes to light, strict action, including a fine, will be taken against it. Fine dust particles pose a risk of reaching the lungs According to environmentalists, dust generated by construction and excavation contains extremely fine particles of silica and various geochemical minerals. These particles can mix with the air and reach the lungs through breathing. This can cause problems such as asthma, breathing difficulties, and irritation in the eyes and throat. Therefore, children, the elderly and people with respiratory illnesses need to take special precautions.
