stories.title: Dummy dropped to recreate scene in Shiva Sharma murder case:Forensic team spends an hour at Shraddha's flat, probes accident and suicide angles
stories.summary: Police conducted a scene recreation at Shraddha Dubey's flat in Lucknow's high-profile Shiva Sharma murder case on Friday. The forensic team discreetly recreated the entire incident in the evening over about an hour. During the exercise, a dummy was dropped from a height to examine aspects related to the incident. DCP Central Arpit Vijayvargiya said the forensic team had conducted the scene recreation to gather necessary evidence. This will help the investigation. The accused in the murder case, Shraddha, her sister Rashmi and driver Adil are currently in jail. The incident took place on the night of 9 October at Awadh Green Apartment in Lucknow. Businessman Shiva Sharma died after falling from the fourth floor under suspicious circumstances. Model Shraddha, her sister Rashmi and driver Danish were also present in the flat at the time. All three fled after the incident. Police arrested them in Nagpur. See three photographs... Scientific and Technical Data Collected In the Shiva Sharma murder case, the police recreated the sequence of events while considering all three possibilities-murder, accident and suicide. During the scene recreation, the police and forensic experts collected scientific and technical data related to the incident. The police recreated the circumstances that had existed at the time of the incident in the Shiva Sharma murder case. The physical positions of Shraddha and Shiva at the time of the incident were estimated. What happened before that was also examined. A dummy was dropped from a height based on the body's weight and height. The distance of the fall, the angle and the point where the body struck the ground were analysed. After collecting important evidence during the investigation, the police proceeded with further action. Evidence gathered in police investigation so far points to murder The evidence gathered by police so far in businessman Shiva Sharma's murder case points to murder. However, Shraddha Dubey and the other accused believe that he died by suicide because he was in debt. The police investigation has so far found marks of physical torture on Shiva Sharma's body. These include burns from cigarettes and injury marks. Evidence was found that lipstick had been applied to Shiva's face, stomach and back at the time of the incident. This was also confirmed during the questioning of accused Shraddha Dubey and her other associates: immediately before the incident, Shiva was in a semi-naked state. He was forced to dance. The three accused were questioned separately Accused Shraddha attempted to destroy one of her mobile phones in Nepal, but the other phone used, hotel checks and travel location data have become part of the police records. The fact that accused Shraddha Dubey, Rashmi Dubey and driver Danish fled to Nepal immediately after the incident and kept changing their locations is strong circumstantial evidence against them. The police questioned the accused-Shraddha, Rashmi and Danish-separately and then face to face. Several discrepancies were found in their statements. Statements from the apartment maid revealed a pattern of continued mental and physical harassment of Shiva Sharma.

stories.title: Keshav says he is unhappy with many things:But now is the time to focus on Mission 2027 and move on
stories.summary: At the BJP's state-level workshop in Lucknow, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya gave party workers the formula for victory in 'Mission 2027'. While Keshav Maurya spoke openly about the workers' grievances, CM Yogi issued strict instructions in a warning tone regarding the revision of electoral rolls (SSR/SIR). Keshav Maurya said- "There are many things that I do not understand either, and I am not satisfied either. When many workers are upset, they voice their grievances on media forums. There are many things that I do not understand either, and I am not happy with them either. But at this time, forget everything else and focus on 'Mission 2027'. We have to form a BJP government in the state for the third consecutive time." Citing figures from the last two Assembly elections, Keshav Maurya cautioned the party workers- He said, "We need to focus on why our vote shifted to the SP in 2022 and how to bring that vote back in favour of the BJP." Chief Minister's warning-set aside all work to get names added Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath urged workers to remain alert, saying, "The special summary revision (SSR) of the electoral roll is the final opportunity before the Assembly election. Workers should set aside all other work for a month and focus on getting names added; otherwise, they will regret it later." The Chief Minister said, "There are 1.27 crore Hindu voters whose names are missing from the electoral roll. The names of 66 lakh voters are included in the gram panchayat list but not in the Assembly voter list. Gram pradhans had their names added to the panchayat list, but not to the Assembly list. Now, the Assembly list should be prepared on the basis of the panchayat list. As many as 55 lakh people are benefiting from government schemes, but their names are not recorded in the electoral roll." BJP's Mega Campaign: Target of 50 New Voters at Every Booth Cooperation Minister JPS Rathore has once again been given charge of election management. He said the Election Commission would publish the draft electoral roll on 17 November 2026. The claims and objections process will run from 17 November to 16 December 2026. During this one-month period, the BJP will run its 'Add Voters Campaign'. stories.title: Pawan Khera alleges ₹17,542 crore tender scam in UP:6 companies formed cartel; BJP leaders accused of shielding them
stories.summary: Senior Congress leader and national spokesperson Pawan Khera levelled serious allegations against the Uttar Pradesh government, accusing it of corruption, tender-fixing and protecting mafia figures from a particular community. He claimed that six companies had colluded to divide up tenders worth ₹17,542 crore in the state. Each company bid for three packages, and each was awarded the tender for one package. He alleged that the companies were being protected by senior BJP leaders. The Congress will continue to make revelations in the matter over the coming months. Khera said the bureaucracy was dominant in Uttar Pradesh and that there was no check on corruption. He said this was because the state's Chief Minister and those running the government were looking towards Delhi instead of Lucknow. The people of the state were paying the price for the ongoing tussle between Delhi and Lucknow. He said the state had been facing this situation since 2017. He also targeted the chief minister for taking part in the protest Pawan Khera took a jibe at the chief minister for joining the protest. He said, "The head of the Uttar Pradesh government had said a few days ago that anyone who attended Rahul Gandhi's protest on 1 November would not get a government job. But just a few hours later, he himself went out to protest. You can understand what his future holds. He is now going to be out of a job. The work of removing him from his job has been done by '2G'. '2G' means two Gujaratis-Amit Shah and Narendra Modi." He said this was the first chief minister from the BJP to openly speak out against Narendra Modi and Amit Shah's SIR. He has realised what is going to happen to him next. That is why he has come out to protest. Accused of dividing tenders among six companies Questioning the tender process, Khera said the entire matter involved cartelisation. Six companies secured the tenders under a mutual agreement. He claimed that tenders worth ₹17,542 crore were divided equally among the six companies. Each company bid for exactly three packages, and each received one package. He said the companies had already reached an agreement that the company awarded the tender would not face a complaint or court appeal from the other companies. This is what is known as cartelisation. He claimed that similar irregularities had occurred in the Jhansi, Farrukhabad and Jewar packages as well. Khera said, "This is a misuse of Uttar Pradesh taxpayers' money. Every company has a senior BJP leader as its patron. The question of how much money went to which patron in this ₹17,542 crore tender will echo across Uttar Pradesh in the coming months. We will make revelations in this matter every day. The bidding process for a tender is merely a pretence. It is decided in advance who will be awarded the tender." He alleged that the state's commissioners had become agents and that senior BJP leaders were playing the role of commission agents. The Congress will ensure that answers are provided in this matter. Allegation of a ₹10,000 crore scam in medicine prices Pawan Khera also attacked the government over the procurement and pricing of medicines. He claimed that a ₹10,000 crore scam had taken place in the medicines sector. A medicine costing ₹2,700 is being sold for ₹27,000. He said the Supreme Court had also commented on medicine prices and described it as daylight robbery. Despite this, the government had not fixed accountability. He said medicines are needed by poor and ordinary people. People cut back on their needs to raise money to buy medicines. In such a situation, this kind of irregularity in medicine prices raises serious questions. Questions also raised over theft of Ram temple offerings Khera raised the issue of the alleged theft of offerings at the Ram temple and said that two years ago, the Prime Minister had inaugurated the temple after sidelining the saints. Who will now answer for the allegations of theft of offerings at the temple? He said people save money for the opportunity to see the deity and make offerings just as they save for medicines. Citing the example of Rajasthan, he said he had seen people there saving money for pilgrimages. Said-A poor man's son will drive an e-rickshaw, while the deputy CM's son will drive a Fortuner Khera also targeted Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak over his statement on the issue of employment. He said that when the state's youth demand jobs, they are advised to drive e-rickshaws. Taking a jibe, he said, "Amit Shah's son will run the BCCI, Brajesh Pathak's son will drive a Fortuner and a poor man's son will drive an e-rickshaw. This is what our Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak has said. We feel ashamed to hear that there are such people in our politics, but they are not even ashamed to make such statements." Accused of protecting strongmen On the issue of law and order, Kheda said the government talks about consigning mafiosi and strongmen to the dust, but itself protects such people. He alleged that there are several strongmen in the state who have the Chief Minister's blessing. He said the Congress had repeatedly offered to provide evidence about such people. The government should state how many such strongmen it had taken action against. He said every child in the state knows the names of those who enjoy the Chief Minister's patronage. Uttar Pradesh breaks record in spending on PR Kheda also questioned the state government's publicity budget. He said that earlier, questions were raised in Delhi about Prime Minister Narendra Modi's PR budget, but it was now being heard that Uttar Pradesh had broken his record as well. He said, "All show, no substance. Those who have nothing to show are the ones who decorate their shops the most. You need to spend on PR only when you have nothing to show." He claimed that Uttar Pradesh leads all states in the country in spending on PR. Now accused of turning even gods against each other Khera targeted the BJP over religious issues, saying that people used to be pitted against Hindus and Muslims, but now even gods are being pitted against one another. He said every person has their own faith. Some believe in one god, while others believe in Allah or Jesus. Earlier, other religions were mocked, and now attempts are being made to pit Hindu deities against one another. He said-If Delhi's arrogance is to be broken, a message must be sent from Lucknow Khera said that if a message had to be sent to Delhi, it would have to begin in Lucknow. That was why the Congress had come to Lucknow, he said. He said, "If Delhi's arrogance is to be broken, make the people of Lucknow walk. Their arrogance will be shattered. The entire party is riding the horse of arrogance." He said every government makes mistakes. Acknowledging a mistake is a sign of greatness, but instead of accepting its mistakes, this government takes action. When journalists show the truth, it wants to prevent them from practising journalism. On the Owaisi-Chandrashekhar alliance, he said-Now, 'Owaisi in your courtyard' When asked about the alliance between Asaduddin Owaisi and Chandrashekhar Azad, Khera replied in a filmi style, "I am Tulsi in your courtyard. Now a film is being made in Lucknow-Owaisi in your courtyard." On Rahul Gandhi's challenge, Khera says PM is afraid of debate Asked about Rahul Gandhi's allegations of phone-tapping and his challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi to a debate, Khera said Rahul Gandhi had been challenging the Prime Minister to a debate for the past 20 days, but he was not coming forward. He said the Prime Minister should bring a teleprompter and debate. Khera claimed that Rahul Gandhi has information about the Prime Minister's foreign relations and his ties with China, the United States and Israel. He also referred to political developments involving Donald Trump in the United States and Benjamin Netanyahu in Israel. On the question of a debate in Parliament, he said, "When I first entered Parliament as an MP, I waited for 22 days to see both of them in the House. The Prime Minister comes to Parliament, but does not come to the House. There will be a debate only when he comes to the House." Spoke on alliance with SP - talks ongoing, will reach a conclusion soon On the alliance with the Samajwadi Party, Pawan Khera said talks were ongoing and that they would soon reach a conclusion on the alliance. Khera said, "You say every time that we delay things, but this time the right thing will certainly be announced at the right time. This is our promise to all of you."

stories.title: Car tyre bursts in Fatehpur leading to horrific accident:Vehicle overturns 3 times, falls 30 feet from overbridge; JE dies, friend critical
stories.summary: A Public Works Department (PWD) junior engineer (JE) was killed in a road accident in Fatehpur on Friday afternoon. The tyre of his speeding car burst on National Highway 2, causing the vehicle to go out of control. It overturned three times on the highway, crossed the divider and crashed into the railing on the opposite side. The impact was so strong that the car's windscreen shattered, and the 40-year-old engineer was thrown around 30 feet below the overbridge. He died on the spot. His friend, who was travelling with him, was seriously injured. The police took him to a Community Health Centre (CHC). From there, he was referred to the district hospital for further treatment. The accident took place around 1:30 pm in the Khaga Kotwali area, about 30 kilometres from the district headquarters. The engineer's family is devastated by his death. Check visuals below : Now read the full story in detail - Rahul Singh (40), a resident of Allahpur in Prayagraj, had been posted as a JE in the PWD in Fatehpur for around three years. He is married and his family lives in Prayagraj. On Friday afternoon, he was travelling to Fatehpur in his Swift Dzire car. His friend Shubham Kumar, a resident of Fatehpur, was also with him. At around 1:30 p.m., the car reached the overbridge on Khaga's eastern bypass when its front tyre burst with a loud bang. Injured friend recounts the accident in full Injured Shubham Singh said Rahul was driving the car and he was seated beside him. As soon as the tyre burst, the car went out of control. It crossed the divider on the highway, overturned three times and crashed straight into the railing. The impact was so severe that the car's window glass shattered. Rahul was thrown out of the car and fell directly onto the service lane below the bridge. Chaos broke out on the highway after the accident. A crowd of passers-by gathered. As soon as the information was received, police from Khaga Kotwali reached the spot. Police pulled the injured Shubham out of the car and took him to Khaga CHC by ambulance. He was referred from there to a medical college for better treatment. Police took the JE's body into custody and sent it for a post-mortem examination. They also informed the family about the accident. As soon as they received the news, the family members left for Fatehpur, crying inconsolably. Police had the car removed from the highway and restored normal traffic. Sanjay Pandey, in-charge of Khaga police station, said the family of the deceased assistant engineer had been informed about the accident. PWD officials and colleagues also reached the hospital and post-mortem house after receiving the information.

stories.title: Raja Bhaiya backs 'Bantoge to Katoge' slogan:Posters showing Lord Ram blessing Akhilesh Yadav put up in Kashi
stories.summary: Political activity has increased in Uttar Pradesh, with statements by leaders, posters supporting and opposing political parties, and action against Congress workers making headlines. Kunda MLA Raja Bhaiya supported Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's slogan, 'Bantoge to Katoge' (If you divide, you will be cut). He said the slogan was absolutely right and every Hindu needed to understand its message. He also claimed that Hindus made up 23% of Pakistan's population when the country was formed, but their share has now fallen to less than 1%. Posters showing Lord Ram supporting Akhilesh Yadav in Varanasi Posters supporting Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav have been put up in Varanasi. One poster shows Lord Ram placing his hand on Yadav's shoulder, while another shows Mata Shabari offering him berries. The posters were put up by Dr Alok Saurabh, state vice-president of the Samajwadi Adhivakta Sabha. SP calls Owaisi and Chandrashekhar Azad's alliance BJP's B-team In Rae Bareli, the Samajwadi Party has put up posters targeting the alliance between Asaduddin Owaisi and Chandrashekhar Azad. The posters call them the BJP's 'B-team' and say, "The BJP finished the BSP, now it is their turn." UP Youth Congress suspends 68 leaders The Uttar Pradesh Youth Congress has suspended 68 office-bearers for not attending Rahul Gandhi's rally in Delhi. Those suspended include 12 district presidents, three state vice-presidents, 33 state general secretaries and 18 state secretaries. Congress spokesperson Haseeb Ahmed said that not attending the rally was treated as an act of indiscipline. The action was taken on this basis. Posters target BJP over roads and crime in Sultanpur Posters targeting the BJP have also appeared in Sultanpur. They mention broken roads, rising accidents, mafias and gang wars, and increasing crime in the area.

stories.title: Brick kiln owner beaten to death in Baghpat:Uncle and his cop son attack him over land dispute, strike his chest repeatedly
stories.summary: A brick kiln owner was murdered in Baghpat on Friday morning. His uncle and two cousins allegedly attacked him with bricks around 10:30 am. They hit him several times in the chest before fleeing when nearby residents reached the spot after hearing the noise. Police took the businessman to a community health centre, where doctors declared him dead. The incident took place in the Chhaprauli police station area, around 35 km from the district headquarters. The deceased's brother is the current village head. Murder linked to ₹2 lakh dispute According to preliminary information, the murder is linked to a dispute over ₹2 lakh. Police are investigating the case and searching for the three accused. See two pictures Now understand the full case Sanjeev (45) lived with his family in Halalpur village. He owned a brick kiln in the village. His family consists of his wife, Anjali, and his 18-year-old son, Dhruv. Sanjeev's elder brother, Sudhir, is currently the village head. Villagers said Sanjeev had been involved in a long-standing dispute with his uncle, Udairaj, over ₹2 lakh. Udairaj and his wife have two sons. The elder son is Sunny, who is in the police and is currently posted in Lucknow. He had come home on leave. The younger son, Aryan, helps his father with farming. Bricks Used to Attack Him After Knocking Him to the Ground At around 10:30 a.m. on Friday, Sanjeev was at a brick kiln near the village. At the same time, accused Udairaj arrived from his field with a tractor-trolley loaded with sugarcane. His two sons, Sunny and Aryan, were with him. During this time, Sanjeev and his uncle Udairaj again had an argument over money at the kiln. Before long, the two began fighting. Udairaj then joined his sons in knocking Sanjeev to the ground. They then repeatedly struck him on the chest with bricks from the same kiln. Sanjeev was left bleeding profusely and writhing in pain. Hearing the commotion, farmers working in nearby fields reached the spot. The accused fled when they saw people approaching. The villagers lifted Sanjeev and informed the police. Died before reaching hospital Personnel from Chhaprauli police station reached the scene and took Sanjeev, who was in agony, to the Chhaprauli community health centre. Doctors declared him dead as soon as they examined him. The family was thrown into turmoil after receiving news of the murder. Family members created a ruckus and demanded the arrest of the accused. Sanjeev's wife and son are inconsolable after the murder. Chhaprauli Station House Officer Prabhakar Kentura said the body had been sent for a post-mortem examination. A case will be registered on the family's complaint. Raids are being conducted to arrest the accused.

stories.summary: Defence Minister and Lucknow MP Rajnath Singh will inaugurate the newly built Divya Sanskriti Bhawan at the Brahma Kumaris' Rajyoga Training Centre in Gulzar Upvan on Sultanpur Road on Friday. Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak will also attend the event. The programme will begin at 11:30 am. Rajnath Singh will travel directly from the airport to the venue. He is scheduled to return to Delhi immediately after the programme. Free Rajyoga meditation training for people BK Radha Didi, in-charge of the Brahma Kumaris' Lucknow sub-zone, said the organisation is celebrating 90 years since its establishment and 72 years of spiritual services in Lucknow as part of Navdashakotsav. People will be offered free training in Rajyoga meditation at Divya Sanskriti Bhawan. Spiritual programmes will also be held at the centre. There are also plans to build an auditorium with a seating capacity of 2,000 people in the future. Several schemes to be launched during the next visit Rajnath Singh is likely to visit Lucknow again on 23 or 24 November. During the visit, he may inaugurate the Saumitra Vihar scheme and the Daliganj flyover. The foundation stone is also proposed to be laid for a six-lane flyover over the Gomti, to be built from Baikunth Dham to La Martiniere College at a cost of around ₹70 crore. In addition, the foundation-laying ceremony for the embankment and flood pumping station in Faizullaganj will be held. Keys will be handed over to the allottees of 110 PM homes in Basant Kunj, while allotment letters will be given to the plot owners of IT City. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will also be present at these events.

stories.title: BJP wants to add voters from other states:Akhilesh Yadav alleges plan to drive voters away from polling booths on election day
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Friday accused the BJP of planning to add voters from other states to the voter lists in place of those whose names have been deleted. He said the BJP wanted to bring people from Madhya Pradesh, Bihar, Uttarakhand and other states and get them registered as voters in Delhi and other places where voters had shifted. Yadav made these claims during a press conference in Lucknow. Before the press conference, he held a review meeting for 86 unreserved assembly constituencies. District presidents, along with assembly constituency presidents and party aspirants, attended the meeting. Akhilesh claims votes were deleted using fake signatures Yadav said the Samajwadi Party had already announced how many thousand votes would be deleted in Pilibhit. Following this, two Sub-Divisional Magistrates (SDMs) were removed from their posts. He also claimed that more than 100 Form 7 applications had been submitted in Lucknow with the same signature. He alleged that voters' names were deleted using the signature of the Samajwadi Party's city president. Questions Election Commission over deletion of 1.27 crore votes Yadav questioned the coordination between the government and the Election Commission. He said the Opposition was not informed about the deletion of votes, while the Chief Minister knew that 1.27 crore votes had been deleted. He further claimed that 31,000 votes had been deleted in every assembly constituency. "If we go by the number of votes, the BJP has lost," he said. Read Akhilesh Yadav's key points... Conspiracy to drive voters away from polling booths on voting day Akhilesh accused the BJP of preparing to create disruptions even on polling day. He said the BJP's plan was to drive voters away from the booth when they went to cast their votes, telling them that their vote was not registered there. They would then be left searching for the booth where their vote was registered. Policemen could even come to my press conference posing as journalists On Rahul Gandhi's phone-tapping allegations, Akhilesh said he feared that policemen might have come posing as journalists. He had caught one in this very room once. Netaji had once held a press conference saying that their phones were being tapped, so it was possible. Anything is possible today. Asked whether difficulties in the alliance would increase or ease, Akhilesh said that he and the Congress were ready. The BJP would lose on the day the election date was announced.

stories.title: SP MP calls Durga Puja and Kanwar Yatra 'hypocrisy':Demands ban, says 50-km journeys serve no purpose and cause blisters
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party MP from Pratapgarh S.P. Singh Patel, said, ‘Durga Puja and the Kanwar pilgrimage are a sham; they should be stopped. People buy idols for Durga Puja, bring them home and worship them. A week later, they throw them into a dirty drain. Tell me, will the goddess bless you or curse you? This tradition should end.’ He said: Carrying a kanwar for 50-50 kilometres achieves nothing. Instead, it leaves your feet covered in blisters. It would be better to offer water at the village temple. If you have a picture of Bhole Baba, simply fold your hands before it and you will receive his blessings. The Samajwadi Party MP made these remarks on Thursday. He had gone to inspect Jalser Ganj station. His video emerged at 9 a.m. this morning. Opposition to Dhirendra Krishna Shastri's religious discourse Earlier, the Samajwadi Party MP had opposed Pandit Dhirendra Krishna Shastri's Shri Ram Katha, scheduled to be held in Kunda, Pratapgarh, from 17 November. The MP said, "My opposition is not to any individual, but to the alleged indecent remarks against deities and women." Using derogatory language about Lord Ram and Lord Krishna and making objectionable remarks against women cannot be the language of a saint. It is not right to have such a person deliver a religious discourse or to honour him. Leaders' statements about deities Swami Prasad had said: Shri Ram lacks the power to punish those who steal offerings Former Cabinet minister Swami Prasad Maurya had said in Ghazipur on 25 June, "If Lord Ram had any power, the thief would have been reduced to ashes the moment he committed the theft. But not even a hair on that thief's head was harmed." Referring to Lord Hanuman, Swami Prasad said, "A small monkey born on Earth swallowed the Sun God. Do we study to put an end to this ignorance?" Citing the thoughts of Gautam Buddha, he said, "Do not believe something merely because it is written in a scripture. First, test it against the standards of your own mind. Believe it only if it stands that test." SP MLA Iqbal Mahmood called Kanwariyas "goons and thugs" On 21 July 2025, former Samajwadi Party cabinet minister and Sambhal MLA Nawab Iqbal Mahmood said, “These people, who are openly engaging in hooliganism and bullying on the streets, are not devotees of Shiva but hooligans. Going by the way they are behaving, they will go to hell, not heaven. If our government is formed, there will be a separate route for Shiva devotees, where they will face no difficulties.” Indrajit Saroj said-If temples had power, plunderers like Ghaznavi and Ghori would not have entered the country Samajwadi Party MLA Inderjit Saroj said in Kaushambi on 14 April 2025, "If India's temples had possessed power, raiders such as Muhammad bin Qasim, Mahmud of Ghazni and Muhammad Ghori would not have entered the country." He asked, "What were the gods and goddesses doing at that time? They were not powerful." He said, "Our god is Ambedkar."

stories.title: Action against Congress workers who did not attend Rahul's rally:List of 68 names proposed for expulsion in UP surfaces; party calls it fake
stories.summary: The party has taken major action against Youth Congress office-bearers who did not attend Rahul Gandhi's rally. Show-cause notices have been issued to office-bearers of the Uttar Pradesh Youth Congress. Some media reports claimed that 68 office-bearers had been suspended for being absent from the rally. However, the Congress called the reports of the office-bearers' suspension fake. Kunwar Nishad, in charge of the Congress media cell, said, "No office-bearer has been suspended. The office-bearers concerned have only been issued show-cause notices." The Congress had organised the "Save the Vote, Save the Country" rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan on 1 November. Youth Congress office-bearers had been instructed to attend it. A digital system had also been put in place to record attendance at the rally, through which records were prepared of office-bearers who had arrived from different states. Claim that 68 office-bearers were being suspended In fact, reports circulated that 68 Youth Congress office-bearers had been suspended based on a statement by state Congress spokesperson Haseeb Ahmed. It was claimed that the Youth Congress national president had taken action, considering absence from the Delhi rally an act of organisational indiscipline. The circulated list was said to include the names of 3 state vice-presidents, 33 state general secretaries, 18 state secretaries, one joint secretary, one social media co-ordinator and 12 district presidents. The names included state vice-president Jitesh Kumar Mishra, state general secretaries Nishant Rastogi and Anubhav Singh, and state secretary Ayush Maurya. There had also been a claim that Prayagraj district president Saurabh Pandey had been suspended. The reasoning given was that Rahul Gandhi had held the 'Goonj' programme in Prayagraj, yet the district president had not attended the rally in Delhi. Digital system was in place to record attendance at the rally The Congress held the 'Save the Vote, Save the Country' rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan on 1 November. Youth Congress office-bearers had been instructed to attend it. The organisation had also set up a digital system to record attendance. Through this system, a record was prepared of the attendance of office-bearers who had arrived from different states. Workshop under way at the Uttar Pradesh Congress headquarters A one-day workshop is being held at the Uttar Pradesh Congress headquarters on Friday. Its objective is to identify issues related to public welfare and formulate a strategy for effective protests and agitation against the government over them. Senior Congress leaders Pawan Khera and Abhay Dubey, Uttar Pradesh Congress in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam, state president Aradhana Mishra 'Mona' and other leaders will address the workshop. Questions were raised within the party after reports emerged that 68 Youth Congress office-bearers had been suspended ahead of the workshop. However, the Congress denied this and clarified that the office-bearers concerned had been issued show-cause notices, not suspended.

stories.title: Meerut IPS officer Aditi Singh to marry Haryana IAS officer:Father doctor, mother clerk; one of the country's top 100 officers
stories.summary: Aditi Singh, IAS officer from Meerut in Uttar Pradesh, will tie the knot today. She will take the seven pheras with Haryana IAS officer Vivev Arya. It was because of this relationship that Aditi Singh was transferred from the Himachal Pradesh cadre to the Haryana cadre. By coincidence, both were posted in Panchkula district. Before the wedding, the haldi and lagni ceremonies were held in Badhra, Bhiwani, from 10 to 12 November. Learn who IPS officer Aditi Singh is About ADC Vivek Arya... Relationship changed state, posted in the same district After being selected for the UPSC, IPS officer Aditi Singh was initially allotted the Himachal Pradesh cadre. However, after her marriage was arranged with Haryana-cadre IAS officer Vivek Arya, she was allotted the Haryana cadre under an inter-cadre transfer. By coincidence, both officers were also posted in Panchkula district, where one is in charge of the administration and the other of law and order.

stories.title: Mother and daughter fall while boarding moving train:Woman trapped in gap; RPF rescues her in 20 seconds
stories.summary: A mother and daughter slipped while trying to board a moving train at Kanpur Central railway station. The young woman fell onto the platform and was rescued by Railway Protection Force (RPF) personnel. Her mother, however, was dragged for around 10 metres before falling into the gap between the train and the platform. RPF personnel asked passengers to pull the emergency chain, bringing the train to a halt within around 20 seconds. By then, four coaches had passed the woman. She was subsequently pulled out from the gap. Woman suffers serious head and facial injuries The woman sustained serious injuries to her head and face in the accident. The entire incident was captured on the station's CCTV cameras. See three pictures... Mother and daughter try to board moving train in haste According to the RPF, the injured woman has been identified as Kalawati Devi, wife of Kamal Rai and a resident of Madhopur Chhata in Bihar's Sheohar district. On Thursday, Kalawati Devi reached Platform 9 of Kanpur Central railway station with her daughter, Sukoon Kumari. At the same time, train number 12566, the Bihar Sampark Kranti Express, began pulling out of the station. In a hurry, both women tried to board the moving train. Kalawati Devi lost her footing and fell into the gap between the train and the platform. RPF personnel prevent daughter from falling under moving train At the time of the incident, RPF sub-inspectors Hemraj Meena and Anil Kumar Gautam were patrolling the station. On seeing the woman fall, both rushed to the spot and attempted to rescue her. They alerted passengers on the train and asked them to pull the emergency chain, bringing it to a halt. Kalawati Devi was then safely pulled out of the gap and brought onto the platform. Her daughter also fell onto the platform while trying to board the moving train. RPF personnel intervened in time and prevented her from slipping under the train. She sustained minor injuries. Bihar Sampark Kranti Express halted during rescue operation Kalawati Devi suffered serious injuries to her head and face. The RPF immediately shifted her to hospital for treatment and informed the police about the incident. The Bihar Sampark Kranti Express remained at the station for some time while the rescue operation was carried out and the injured woman was taken to hospital. This caused some inconvenience to passengers.

stories.title: Posters supporting Akhilesh Yadav appear in Varanasi:Lord Ram shown with hand on SP chief's shoulder; message reads, 'SP government will be formed with God's blessings'
stories.summary: A poster put up in Varanasi in support of Samajwadi Party national president Akhilesh Yadav has sparked discussion. Put up by a Samajwadi Party leader in the Varuna area, the poster shows Lord Ram placing his hand on Akhilesh Yadav's shoulder. In another scene, Lord Ram is seen feeding berries to Mata Shabari. The poster reads, 'A clarion call from the city of Shri Kashi Vishwanath; with Lord Ram's blessings, a Samajwadi government will be formed.' Dr Alok Saurabh, state vice-president of the Samajwadi Adhivakta Sabha, had the poster put up. He has also released a video of it. Message of social harmony and equality through the poster Dr Alok Saurabh said that Kashi is the land of Lord Vishwanath and that Lord Shri Ram's blessings are with everyone. The purpose of depicting the episode involving Mata Shabari and Lord Shri Ram in the poster is to convey a message of love, social harmony and equality. This episode from the Ramayana teaches society the values of mutual love and equality. He said: Ram does not belong to any one party or class Dr Alok Saurabh said that socialist ideology seeks to secure dignity and rights for those at the bottom of society. It believes in taking everyone along and according them due respect, instead of discriminating based on religion and caste. Taking aim at the BJP, he said that BJP leaders try to portray themselves as the custodians of Hinduism, whereas Lord Shri Ram does not belong to any one party or class but is worshipped by everyone. Lord Shri Ram's blessings are upon all. When the Lord wishes, people will also have his darshan. Akhilesh has announced that he will go to Ayodhya on 12 December Former minister and Samajwadi Party leader Pawan Pandey had announced in recent days that Akhilesh Yadav would visit Ayodhya on 12 December. Before offering prayers to Ram Lalla there, he would also visit Hanumangarhi. Following the announcement, political statements intensified across the state. Several leaders, including BJP leaders, questioned Akhilesh's announcement of his Ayodhya visit, linking it to politics. Akhilesh Yadav had earlier said that he would offer prayers to Ram Lalla after the construction of the Kedareshwar Temple in Etawah was completed.

stories.title: Girl gets maths teacher killed by boyfriend:She alleged he had made obscene photos of her; throat slit and 'OP Yadav rapist' written on blackboard
stories.summary: The murder of a maths teacher in Agra has been solved. A former student of the coaching centre had him killed by her boyfriend. The student alleged that the teacher had created obscene photographs of her and was blackmailing her. The accused killed the teacher by slitting his throat at the coaching centre on 2 November. After the crime, he wrote 'OP Yadav rapist rapist' on the blackboard and fled with the teacher's mobile phone and scooter. Four days after the crime, the body of teacher Om Prakash Yadav (50) was found in the basement of the coaching centre. There were deep wounds on the body. His throat had been slit. When the police examined the teacher's call records, they found that he had been in constant contact with one mobile number. The investigation revealed that the number belonged to the teacher's former student. When the police detained the student and questioned her, she confessed to the crime. The case falls under the jurisdiction of Jagdishpura police station. Teacher had lived in Agra for 30 years and had not married Teacher Om Prakash Yadav was originally from Kathika village in the Rasoolabad police station area of Kanpur Dehat. He had been living in Agra for 30 years. He had not married. He had built his own house in Awas Vikas Colony. He taught at Shivalik Cambridge School in Sector 7. He also ran a coaching centre at VS Plaza in Sector 3. Went to the coaching centre on 2 November and never returned He reached the coaching centre on 2 November but did not return home. His family searched for him, but could not find him. On 6 November, people living nearby informed the police after a strong stench began coming from the coaching centre. Following this, a team from the Jagdishpura police station reached BS Plaza. Murder case uncovered after stench emerged four days later Police opened the door of the coaching centre and searched inside, where they found the teacher's body. The body was mutilated, and a large amount of blood had spread around it and had dried. 'OP Yadav rapist' was found written in marker on the coaching centre's blackboard. Police had the body post-mortem examined. The preliminary report found nine injury marks on the teacher's body, seven of them caused by a sharp weapon. Police traced the student through call records The investigation revealed that the teacher's mobile phone and scooter were missing. Police then examined the call records for his mobile number, which led them to a girl. She initially misled police, then said he had been blackmailing her Police called the student in for questioning. She initially misled them, saying, "Sir was a very good person." But when police showed her the call records and messages, she began crying. She said the teacher had created obscene photographs of her using Snapchat. The student said, "He used to blackmail me by showing me the photographs. He used to send obscene messages. I had become very worried by the teacher's behaviour. I then told my boyfriend, Nikhil, about it." Teacher reprimanded her boyfriend, so she had him killed The student said Nikhil went to the coaching centre with a knife to meet the teacher on 2 November. He tried to reason with the teacher and told him not to harass his girlfriend. But the teacher reprimanded Nikhil. While the teacher was scolding him, Nikhil pulled a knife from his pocket and slit the teacher's throat. As soon as he was attacked in the throat, the teacher fell, bleeding onto the floor and began writhing in pain. Nikhil then repeatedly stabbed him in the chest, head, and neck. He died. Nikhil fled the scene after the attack.

stories.title: Preparations underway at 84 ghats in Kashi for Chhath festival:Over 100 changing rooms to be set up, cleaning planned across 8-km ghat stretch
stories.summary: The Chhath festival begins across the country today with Nahay-Khay. In view of the four-day festival, the Varanasi Municipal Corporation is making arrangements at 84 ghats spread across an area of 8 kilometres. As part of this, the municipal commissioner inspected the ghats on Thursday and issued the necessary directions. The Municipal Corporation has begun removing waste from the ghats, along with cleaning the silt. Municipal Corporation PRO Sandeep Srivastava said that barricading was also being carried out at all the ghats, and warning boards were being installed at those considered dangerous. Changing rooms are also being built for women at the ghats. Comprehensive arrangements across an 8-kilometre area Sandeep Srivastava said, "Our ghat area along the Ganga stretches across eight kilometres. Adequate numbers of sanitation workers have been deployed there, and arrangements have been made to collect waste several times a day. The mayor and municipal commissioner are also patrolling day and night, personally conducting on-site inspections and issuing instructions." On all these points, the municipal corporation is arranging adequate lighting at all the ghats. The ghats will be levelled and kept free of silt. If any silt remains or any area is still wet, sand is being filled into sacks and placed there so that people do not face any difficulty while moving around. More than 100 changing rooms being built at the ghats Sandeep Srivastava said that changing rooms had been arranged at the ghats. An adequate number of these changing rooms is being built for women at every ghat. As far as security is concerned, warning boards have been put up at all the dangerous ghats. Ropes will also be tied there so that people can bathe safely. The Municipal Corporation is making all these preparations. Chhath Puja to be held at all ghats; none will be closed Asked whether prayers would not be held at ghats where the Ganga is particularly deep, Sandeep said, "No, no such ghat has been identified. There are some ghats, such as Tulsi Ghat and Lalita Ghat, where the water is deeper." Signage boards are put up there stating, "This is a dangerous ghat; bathe or offer prayers here with caution," along with, "The water is deep; do not go beyond this point." Barricades are also installed in the water to prevent people from going further and ensure their safety. The municipal corporation carries out all these measures.

stories.title: Film on Atiq-Ahmed and Mukhtar Ansari being made in Gorakhpur:Ravi Kishan plays an STF officer who takes down criminals through encounters
stories.summary: Actor and MP Ravi Kishan will now be seen taking on the screen the likes of Atiq Ahmed and Mukhtar Ansari, mafias who once established their dominance in Uttar Pradesh through terror and crime. The Hindi crime thriller film STF: Mission Mafia is currently being shot in Gorakhpur. Ravi Kishan plays an encounter specialist from the Special Task Force (STF) in the film. The story will depict the terror spread by mafias in Uttar Pradesh, their criminal networks, and their elimination. The film's shooting has generated considerable excitement in the city. It is also being widely discussed on social media. See 3 pictures from the shoot... Sets are being prepared in different parts of the city for the film's shoot. Recently, an important scene from the film was shot in the Miyan Bazaar area. As soon as news of this spread, a large number of local people reached the spot. People appeared excited to watch their MP and favourite actor, Ravi Kishan, act in front of the cameras. A crowd remained gathered around the shooting location for a long time. Scenes also filmed at the Boating Centre and Ramgarh Tal The film's shooting is not limited to Miyan Bazaar. Different scenes are also being filmed at the Boating Centre, Ramgarh Tal, and other parts of the city. A few days ago, a crowd of Ravi Kishan's fans gathered at the Boating Centre during filming to see him. People surrounded him from all sides and began taking selfies with him. Fans remained gathered at the shooting location for a long time. The film will portray the STF's action against criminals, encounters, the influence of the mafia in political circles and police action. Along with action, the film will also feature political developments and events linked to the world of crime. It is being described as a big-budget pan-India crime thriller inspired by true events. Ravi Kishan says Gorakhpur will gain lakhs and crores Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, actor and MP Ravi Kishan said the shooting of this film would bring significant economic benefits to Gorakhpur. Business worth lakhs and crores is expected to be generated in the city as a result. More than 30 artists have also received employment opportunities. Considerable enthusiasm for the film is also being seen among young people. He said the film is based on true events and will depict the story of the end of the mafia's reign of terror in Uttar Pradesh. More films will be shot in Gorakhpur in the coming days, giving the city recognition as a film city and creating new employment opportunities for local people. Film on STF's operations made for the first time in Hindi cinema It is being claimed that 'STF: Mission Mafia' is the first film in Hindi cinema to centre on the functioning of the Special Task Force (STF) and its campaign against the mafia. Ravi Kishan's character will be shown working on a mission to dismantle the criminals' network. The story will unfold against the backdrop of the mafia's influence in Uttar Pradesh and the police action taken against them. Five other films and web series also in the pipeline in Gorakhpur The film's shooting is also considered significant for Gorakhpur. Along with promoting film production at the local level, it is expected to create work opportunities for actors, technicians, and others. Filming in the city could further strengthen Gorakhpur's identity as a shooting location. Notably, plans are also reportedly underway to shoot five other Bhojpuri films and web series in Gorakhpur besides this film. This could lead to increased film-related activity in the city in the coming days.

stories.title: Fog blankets 20 districts in UP, temperature drops to 13°C:Air quality deteriorates in 5 cities, Ghaziabad most polluted; cold to intensify after 2 days
stories.summary: Cold is gradually intensifying in Uttar Pradesh. Fog covered 20 cities, including Lucknow, Varanasi, Kanpur, Kushinagar and Ballia, on Friday morning. Visibility in rural areas was so low that it was difficult to see beyond 100 metres. Night-time temperatures have been steadily falling. The lowest temperature, 13°C, was recorded in Hardoi. Pollution is also increasing along with the cold. The air quality in five cities in the state is extremely poor. Ghaziabad was the most polluted city, with an AQI of 338. The AQI was recorded at 328 in Meerut, 311 in Shamli and Noida, and 304 in Bulandshahr. Over the past 24 hours, Hardoi was the coldest city, with a temperature of 13°C. The daytime temperature has also fallen below 32°C. Atul Kumar Singh, a weather scientist in Lucknow, said: A new western disturbance has become active. As a result, strong, cold winds will blow in from the mountains. This could cause daytime and night-time temperatures to fall by 3 to 5 degrees over the next two days. There is no possibility of rain over the next six days. Demolition halted in Ghaziabad; Schools in Noida to operate in hybrid mode Due to pollution, Ghaziabad DM Ravindra Kumar has banned construction and demolition work until 20 November. Meanwhile, schools up to Class 5 in Noida and Greater Noida have been ordered to operate in hybrid mode. This means children can attend school in person or take online classes. What is the Air Quality Index (AQI)? It is a score that indicates the quality of the air and helps us understand whether the air around us is clean or polluted. The AQI measures the levels of pollutants present in the air. The higher the AQI, the more hazardous the air is considered to be, and the greater the health risk. Understand it from the graphic below- How does poor AQI affect our health? When the AQI is poor, pollutants such as PM2.5, PM10, nitrogen dioxide, sulphur dioxide, and ozone in the air can reach deep into our lungs. These particles spread throughout the body through the bloodstream. They can cause several types of health problems, ranging from immediate issues to long-term conditions. This ancient artifact, believed to originate from the rule of Roman Emperor Hadrian between 117 and 138 CE, caught the attention of experts after the children promptly informed their teacher.

As both leaders gear up for the upcoming 2027 Assembly elections, they aim to challenge the BJP's grip on power.

stories.title: Dakota apartment owned by Tribeca Film Festival founders sells after price cut
stories.summary: After nearly ten years of trying to sell their apartment at the Dakota, the couple has finally found a buyer. The apartment was initially listed at $39 million but was later reduced to $12.5 million. Located on Central Park, the spacious unit spans about 6,000 square feet, offering stunning views of the park. The sale comes after significant price cuts and complex negotiations between the former couple.

He highlighted past governance failures, including riots and insecurity, under the Samajwadi Party. Adityanath claimed the state is now safer and riot-free under BJP leadership. He reiterated that security, nationalism, and cultural nationalism would be central themes in upcoming elections.

stories.title: Saffron saree row: West Bengal government to probe claim Kolkata school questioned teacher's dress choice

The charges claim a colleague questioned the teacher for wearing saffron sarees, alleging a dress code violation. Chief minister Suvendu Adhikari indicated potential actions against individuals or the institution if complaints are verified. BJP's Samik Bhattacharya also raised concerns about possible religious conversions at such institutions.

Earlier, his associate, Umar Nisar Dar, was taken down in a separate encounter. Lateef had wounded three CRPF personnel during a recent attack and had evaded capture since then. The authorities reiterated their strong stance against further terrorist activities in the region.

stories.title: Wrongful Death Settlement: Brown family secures $5 million; claims against Walgreens remain pending
stories.summary: The family of Banko Brown, a Black transgender man fatally shot by a security guard, has secured a $5 million settlement related to claims against the guard and his employer. However, the legal battle continues, as the family's lawsuit against Walgreens and Allied Universal Security Services remains unresolved in court.

stories.title: Paul McCartney and Ringo Starr back new Beatles attraction in Liverpool; will support young local artists
stories.summary: Liverpool is set to unveil a major Beatles attraction by 2028, championed by Paul McCartney and Ringo Starr. This expansive 100,000-square-foot venue will replace the Beatles Story at Albert Dock, featuring immersive exhibits designed to boost tourism. A portion of ticket sales will support local artists via the Apple Corps Liverpool Trust, aiming to celebrate young talent and align with the premiere of four Beatles films in April 2028.

stories.title: Michigan woman wins $1 million Powerball prize, plans to pay off her mortgage
stories.summary: Alisa Moore, hailing from Hazel Park, Michigan, recently struck gold by winning a staggering $1 million in the Powerball lottery. She bought her lucky ticket while exiting a Kroger store on October 19. The next day, after thoroughly checking her ticket, she confirmed her fortune. Instead of indulging in luxury, Moore aims to settle her mortgage and wisely invest the leftover amount, showcasing her savvy handling of unexpected wealth.

Guinness Verification Pending: Warren Crawford bowls 243 strikes; fundraiser raises $20,000
stories.summary: Warren Crawford stunned everyone with his astounding bowling prowess, clocking in 243 strikes within a single hour at a charity event that benefitted veterans and first responders. The endeavor successfully garnered around $20,000 in donations. Utilizing a unique two-handed bowling style he honed since childhood, Crawford's incredible achievement now awaits verification from Guinness World Records, all amidst the electrifying support of the audience.

stories.title: Plea alleges Sonia Gandhi used forged papers for 1980 voter entry; court seeks police report

During proceedings, the advocate presented electoral roll records from 1980 to 1983.

stories.title: Roger Daltrey's cancer charity concerts reach 150 shows, raising over £36 million since 2000
stories.summary: The Teenage Cancer Trust celebrated its 150th concert at London's Royal Albert Hall, raising over £36 million. Founded by Roger Daltrey in 2000, the series features numerous well-known musicians supporting young people with cancer. Performers such as Manic Street Preachers and Elbow participated in the recent program curated by Robert Smith. The charity emphasizes the importance of specialized care for patients aged 13 to 24 during treatment.

stories.title: Teens who met on holiday in 1994 reunite 20 years later and marry
stories.summary: It was in the sun-soaked summer of 1994 when David McArdle encountered Jodie while vacationing in Kos, Greece. Their brief encounter ignited a beautiful friendship carried through pen letters for three years. Life scattered them, but fate intervened after twenty years when Jodie reached out to David's mother. Their profound reconnection blossomed into love, culminating in a proposal atop the London Eye.

His potential victory aligns with other momentous leadership changes, reflecting the priorities of newly elected lawmakers eager to push legislative agendas before their official induction.

Their leaders stress the essential need for financial aid from wealthier nations, which contribute most to pollution. This call for unity among these nations is becoming increasingly crucial. Young representatives advocate for climate justice and demand accountability from world leaders, as COP31 seeks to reinforce commitments to effectively tackle climate change.

stories.title: 'Heavens will not fall': SC on ED plea challenging Azam Khan's interim bail
Unvaccinated yellow fever-risk travellers may face six-day quarantine; new airport rules propose changes
stories.summary: India has unveiled draft regulations enhancing quarantine protocols for travelers from yellow fever-affected nations. Unvaccinated arrivals could face quarantine of up to six days at their own expense. Airlines will be responsible for transporting non-compliant passengers to designated facilities. Furthermore, new reporting standards concerning passenger health and travel information will be established for airlines. The health ministry is collecting feedback from all stakeholders on these proposed measures before finalization.

stories.title: Tennessee studio estate where Taylor Swift and Dolly Parton recorded lists for $19.5 million
stories.summary: Dark Horse Estate in Franklin, Tennessee is now on the market for $19.5 million. This unique property features recording facilities and accommodations for artists and guests alike. It has a rich history with over 65 gold and platinum albums recorded by various notable musicians. The estate spans over 10 acres, providing privacy and ample outdoor space for inspiration and relaxation.

stories.title: In just one week, how security forces avenged attack on CRPF personnel in Kulgam
Rare dinosaur discovery: Palaeontologists may uncover new dinosaur species; fossil from Utah to be studied in Raleigh's Dino Lab
stories.summary: The North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences in Raleigh is buzzing with excitement over a rare dinosaur skeleton recently acquired. Dating back 75 million years, and reminiscent of a large ostrich, this find from Utah could represent a new species, subject to further investigation. Visitors have the unique opportunity to view live research in the Dino Lab, offering insights into the diversity of dinosaurs from this area.

stories.title: Caltech robot revolutionizes space: Caltech robot builds structure in space; Space assembly showcases future construction possibilities
stories.summary: A robot developed by researchers at California Institute of Technology constructed a segment of a space structure autonomously. The assembly occurred as part of DARPA's NOM4D programme, testing innovative techniques for space construction. The Autonomous In-Space Tensioned Reflector Assembly robot utilized individual components to build an experimental antenna. Following the launch, the robot successfully coordinated with Earth-based commands to assemble its structure in orbit.

stories.title: NMC asks medical colleges to vet draft rules seeking tighter checks on animal experiments
stories.summary: The National Medical Commission has introduced new draft rules to enhance the ethical treatment of laboratory animals in research. Emphasizing the importance of alternative methods, researchers must prioritize minimizing animal suffering and avoid experiments that could result in prolonged distress. Furthermore, institutions are mandated to appoint veterinarians and form ethics committees to supervise the research. Any breaches could result in significant repercussions, including the potential revocation of registrations.

stories.title: 'Responsibility to banish hatred': Mamdani condemns anti-Indian racism at Diwali event
stories.summary: Mayor Zohran Mamdani addressed rising incidents of racism targeting the Indian-American community during a Diwali celebration. He emphasized the need for collective responsibility in combating hate and ensuring safety for Hindus and Sikhs. Thirteen US lawmakers have requested a federal investigation into a disruption of a Diwali event in Seattle. They referred to troubling patterns of anti-South Asian hate across the country.

stories.title: MacKenzie Scott donated $26 billion freely; four donors put $189 million into named institutes

The discussions are set to occur during the Apec summit in Shenzhen, China. Putin aims to strengthen Russia's diplomatic position while addressing the war in Ukraine. However, there are differing agendas that could complicate the talks, particularly regarding nuclear disarmament.

stories.title: BJP calls Rahul Gandhi 'Mir Jafar of India' over his remarks on economy in US
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi's recent remarks at Columbia University regarding India's economy have drawn criticism from BJP leaders. While he mentioned an impending economic disaster and unemployment issues, BJP officials accused him of spreading anti-India propaganda. They highlighted discrepancies between his views and positive economic indicators such as GDP growth and reduced unemployment rates. BJP spokespersons emphasized the need for leaders to represent India positively abroad.
